title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
description: The DOJ's embrace of fair use for AI training breaks with the White House's own framework, as OpenAI, Microsoft and news groups battle over copyright.
fullContent:
One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

title: ARK Invest Buys $90M in Anthropic Shares While Trimming Ethereum ETF Holdings
description: Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest made a major move into artificial intelligence during Anthropic’s first day on the Nasdaq, purchasing nearly $91 million worth of shares in the newly listed company. At the same time, the investment firm reduced its exposure to Ethereum and Solana staking exchange-traded funds, highlighting another round of portfolio adjustments across its […]
fullContent:
Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest made a major move into artificial intelligence during Anthropic’s first day on the Nasdaq, purchasing nearly $91 million worth of shares in the newly listed company.

At the same time, the investment firm reduced its exposure to Ethereum and Solana staking exchange-traded funds, highlighting another round of portfolio adjustments across its technology and crypto-related holdings. According to ARK’s latest trading disclosures, the firm acquired 934,968 Anthropic shares across six of its actively managed ETFs on Thursday. Based on the stock’s closing price of $97.17, the position was valued at approximately $90.9 million.

The purchases came alongside sales of $2.9 million in 3iQ Ethereum staking ETF holdings and $1.2 million in its Solana staking ETF. The transactions show ARK adding exposure to the AI sector while reducing selected positions linked to digital assets.

ARK Builds Anthropic Exposure Across Six ETFs

ARK distributed its Anthropic purchases across six funds, with the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) accounting for the largest portion. The fund purchased approximately 60% of the total shares acquired, although the position represented only around 0.4% of ARKK’s overall holdings.

The remaining purchases were spread across ARK’s other actively managed ETFs, including its Next Generation Internet, Autonomous Technology & Robotics, Genomic Revolution, Fintech Innovation, and Space Exploration & Innovation funds.

The investment reflects ARK’s continued activity in emerging technology companies. However, the firm’s disclosures do not provide the exact prices at which the Anthropic shares were purchased. The $90.9 million figure represents their value using Thursday’s closing price rather than a confirmed total purchase cost.

ARK’s portfolio strategy also limits the weight of individual holdings, with the firm generally seeking to prevent any single position from exceeding 10% of a fund. This approach can lead to further adjustments when the value of a holding changes significantly relative to other assets.

Anthropic Shares Deliver a Strong Nasdaq Debut

ARK’s investment coincided with a high-profile stock market debut for Anthropic, the company behind the Claude artificial intelligence model.

Trading under the ticker ANT, shares opened at $111.50, approximately 34% above the initial public offering price of $83. The stock later gave back part of its early gains, closing at $97.17, still 17.1% above the IPO price.

Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 each, generating approximately $81.3 billion in offering value. The company had initially indicated a price range of $70 to $78 per share and planned to sell fewer shares, making the final offering larger than originally anticipated.

The total could increase to approximately $93.5 billion if underwriters exercise their option to purchase an additional 147 million shares. A separate planned $26 billion private placement involving major technology companies, including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC, would bring the combined total to approximately $107.3 billion before the additional underwriting option.

ARK Reduces Ethereum and Solana Staking ETF Exposure

While increasing its Anthropic position, ARK also trimmed holdings in two crypto-linked investment products.

The firm sold approximately $2.9 million worth of the 3iQ Ethereum staking ETF and another $1.2 million worth of the 3iQ Solana staking ETF. The reductions came through its ARKW Next Generation Internet and ARKF Blockchain & Fintech Innovation funds.

The underlying cryptocurrencies recorded declines during Thursday’s session. Ethereum fell approximately 1.1%, while Solana slipped 0.7%, according to market data. Meanwhile, the 3iQ Ethereum staking ETF closed 0.4% higher at $6.85, while its Solana counterpart ended the session down 0.3%.

The mixed performance highlights the difference between movements in the underlying tokens and those of investment products tied to them.

ARK Continues to Rebalance Its Portfolio

ARK Invest latest transactions form part of its broader approach to managing exposure across technology, artificial intelligence, and digital assets. The firm regularly adjusts fund weightings as individual holdings change in value, while maintaining its diversification strategy.

The Anthropic purchase represents a notable addition to its AI exposure, but the simultaneous reductions in Ethereum and Solana staking ETFs do not, on their own, establish a wider retreat from the cryptocurrency sector. The firm may continue adjusting its positions as market conditions and portfolio weightings evolve. For now, its latest disclosures show a clear increase in exposure to Anthropic alongside smaller reductions in selected crypto-linked products.

Do you think ARK Invest Anthropic purchase signals growing confidence in AI stocks, or is it simply another portfolio rebalancing move? Could its reductions in Ethereum and Solana staking ETFs point to a change in how the firm approaches crypto-related investments?

title: PayPal Names New CFO, Overhauls Venmo, Crypto and AI Leadership As Three-Year Strategy Takes Shape
description:
PayPal Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:PYPL) announced a major executive leadership reshuffle Friday, appointing a new chief financial officer and senior executives across its Consumer Financial Services & Venmo, Payment Services & Crypto, and artificial intelligence businesses.
The leadership changes follow several months of strategic planning aimed at establishing clear strategies across PayPal’s core businesses, simplifying its operating model and accelerating execution of its three-year growth strategy.
New CFO And Key Leadership Appointments
President and CEO Enrique Lores said the company has made significant progress in defining its competitive strategy and is now shifting its focus toward execution.
Claire Bramley, EVP and chief financial officer: Bramley will join PayPal on Feb. 1,  succeeding Jamie Miller, currently chief financial and operating officer. She joins from Xero, where she has served as CFO since April 2025, helping drive its U.S. expansion and acquisition of payments platform Melio. Previously, she held senior finance positions at Teradata and HP (NYSE:HPQ).
Kartik Mani, president and head of Consumer Financial Services & Venmo: Mani joins from American Express (NYSE:AXP), where he serves as President of Global Network and Partner Services and prior to that led Citi’s Consumer Banking business across Asia and EMEA. He will oversee PayPal’s consumer financial services strategy, including Venmo.
Suzan Kereere, president and head of Payment Services & Crypto: Kereere, currently head of Global Markets, will lead PayPal’s payments and cryptocurrency operations. She succeeds interim leader Jeff Pomeroy, who will continue overseeing Payment Services & Platforms and report to Kereere.
Juan Rio, EVP of AI Business Transformation & Operations: Rio will join on Nov. 30 from Brightstar.AI. He will lead PayPal’s AI transformation, cost simplification and enterprise operational efficiency initiatives, drawing on experience in large-scale business transformations, including the T-Mobile (NASDAQ:TMUS) and Sprint integration.
The company said Frank Keller will continue leading Checkout Solutions & PayPal, including branded checkout.
PayPal also announced that Chief Risk Officer Aaron Webster will depart. Ratinder Bedi, senior vice president of Credit and Fraud Risk, will temporarily lead the risk organization while the company searches for a permanent successor.
Additionally, PayPal appointed Brian J. Lee to its board. Lee brings more than 30 years of financial services experience, including six years as Chief Risk Officer at Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS), which he joined in 1994.
PayPal plans to provide an update on progress against its three-year strategic plans during its fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call.
Analyst Outlook
The stock carries a Hold rating with an average price forecast of $57.91. Recent analyst moves include:
Bernstein: Maintained a Market Perform rating and raised its price forecast to $60 on Nov. 11.
Barclays: Downgraded the stock to Underweight and lowered its price forecast to $53 on Oct. 29.
Morgan Stanley: Maintained a Neutral rating and lowered its price forecast to $60 on Oct. 28.
PYPL Price Action: PayPal Holdings shares were down 3.80% at $54.23 in premarket activity on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: Revolution Medicines Highlights Strong 12-Month Overall Survival Rate for Lead Cancer Drug Regimen
description:
Revolution Medicines, Inc. (NASDAQ:RVMD) on Thursday reported encouraging updated results from its Phase 1/2 RMC-GI-102 open-label study of Rasonque (daraxonrasib) combined with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel (GnP) as a potential first-line treatment for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
The global, commercial-stage oncology company, which focuses on developing medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers, will present the findings during a late-breaking oral session at the EORTC-NCI-AACR (ENA) Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics.
Rasonque Delivers Strong Pancreatic Cancer Response Rates
As of Sept. 28, 2026, 61 patients in the first-line metastatic PDAC cohort received 200 mg of Rasonque plus GnP, reaching a median follow-up of 18.3 months.
The updated analysis showed a confirmed objective response rate of 60.7%, including complete responses in 8.2% of patients.
The regimen achieved a 90.2% disease control rate and a median duration of response of 11.1 months.
Patients also reached a median progression-free survival of 12.8 months and a 12-month overall survival rate of 76.6%.
Consistent Safety Profile Builds On Earlier Data
The combination therapy maintained a safety profile consistent with what researchers previously observed for both Rasonque and GnP.
The update builds on findings that investigators presented at the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) Annual Meeting in April 2026.
In August, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Rasonque for metastatic PDAC, via the agency’s controversial fast-track drug review pilot program.
Revolution Medicines began treating patients in October in its global Phase 3 clinical study, RASolve 308, to evaluate a combination treatment for metastatic lung cancer.
The trial tests the company’s investigational therapy, zoldonrasib, alongside standard care as a first-line treatment for adults with non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer harboring the RAS G12D mutation.
RVMD Price Action: Revolution Medicines shares were up 2.24% at $163.00 during premarket trading on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping
Bitcoin is trading barely above its realized price, the average cost of every coin, and a break below would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023.
This post Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping

Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday.

The price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater.

The margin is thin. The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price.

What the realized price measures

Realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market.

The MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost.

The firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. Bitcoin Magazine Pro’s full realized price chart sits behind a login, so the current level could not be confirmed independently for this report.

“The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit,” the firm wrote. “The margin is thin.”

Outflows and liquidations add to the pressure

The slide has come with heavy selling from funds. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost about $541 million on Thursday, its largest one-day outflow since it launched in January 2024, Bloomberg reported. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total that day.

The selling stands out against the buying earlier in the fall. Institutions piled into bitcoin ETFs through the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record, Bitcoin Magazine reported this week.

Leveraged traders took losses too. More than $700 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and about 86% of them were bets on higher prices. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $200 million of the total.

CoinShares sees range trading through 2027

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop is part of a longer downturn rather than the start of a new one. “I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another,” he said in a note dated Nov. 18.

The note frames Friday’s price action as a late stage of a decline that began well before November. Butterfill pointed to whale selling that weighed on prices from late 2025, expectations of higher interest rates and weakness in technology stocks, all of which have kept buyers cautious.

“Our base case remains range trading around USD 60k to 90k through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives monetary policy room to ease,” he said. “Geopolitics will have a considerable say in that.”

A move through the realized price would put bitcoin near the bottom edge of that range. The firm said holders as a group have not been in loss since early 2023.

A sustained breakout, Butterfill said, would likely require “a change in the policy outlook, renewed whale participation or both.”

This post Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday.

The price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater.

The margin is thin. The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price.

What the realized price measures

Realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market.

The MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost.

The firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. Bitcoin Magazine Pro’s full realized price chart sits behind a login, so the current level could not be confirmed independently for this report.

“The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit,” the firm wrote. “The margin is thin.”

Outflows and liquidations add to the pressure

The slide has come with heavy selling from funds. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost about $541 million on Thursday, its largest one-day outflow since it launched in January 2024, Bloomberg reported. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total that day.

The selling stands out against the buying earlier in the fall. Institutions piled into bitcoin ETFs through the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record, Bitcoin Magazine reported this week.

Leveraged traders took losses too. More than $700 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and about 86% of them were bets on higher prices. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $200 million of the total.

CoinShares sees range trading through 2027

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop is part of a longer downturn rather than the start of a new one. “I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another,” he said in a note dated Nov. 18.

The note frames Friday’s price action as a late stage of a decline that began well before November. Butterfill pointed to whale selling that weighed on prices from late 2025, expectations of higher interest rates and weakness in technology stocks, all of which have kept buyers cautious.

“Our base case remains range trading around USD 60k to 90k through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives monetary policy room to ease,” he said. “Geopolitics will have a considerable say in that.”

A move through the realized price would put bitcoin near the bottom edge of that range. The firm said holders as a group have not been in loss since early 2023.

A sustained breakout, Butterfill said, would likely require “a change in the policy outlook, renewed whale participation or both.”

title: Why Is AMD Stock Falling on Friday?
description:

title: 'GTA 6' sold around 24.5 million copies after its release — and made a lot of money
description:
Grand Theft Auto VI is here at last, and gamers around the world can finally play after it launched Thursday. So far, the game, which takes up a whopping 212GB on your PlayStation5 or Xbox, is receiving rave reviews. GTA 6 is streaming all over Twitch, and the memes, clips and hot takes have been pouring in.
Digital marketing firm Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 generated $2.36 billion in pre-orders and first-day sales, with approximately 24.5 million copies sold following its Thursday release. GTA 6 costs $79.99 for PS5 and Xbox, with an "ultimate" version priced at $99.99. Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two have yet to confirm official sales figures but described demand as "unprecedented."
Players began pre-loading GTA 6 last week, even though they probably had to clear some space on their consoles. Millions of people are expected to take time off work and school to play GTA 6.  Xbox has a doctor's note from DJ Khaled (aka Dr. Xbox) that may be the excuse you need (but you'll probably want to clear it with your boss either way).
PlayStation's network suffered a brief outage Wednesday afternoon as the game became available and players made the required update to their consoles. But since Wednesday evening, it's been smooth sailing. 
Here's what people are saying about GTA VI . Just be warned: there are spoilers ahead for those who haven’t played all the way through yet.

title: Bitcoin Sheds $25,000 in 7 Weeks, but Peter Schiff Says It ‘Hasn’t Gone Down Enough’
description:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) has lost nearly $25,000 in seven weeks, and economist Peter Schiff says the slide still isn’t enough.
Schiff Says Gold’s Drop Is a Buy, Bitcoin’s Is a Sell
"The two biggest differences between what is now happening to gold and Bitcoin are: Gold shouldn’t have gone down at all and Bitcoin hasn’t gone down enough," Schiff noted, adding that gold’s decline looks like a buying opportunity while Bitcoin’s looks like a reason to sell. 
He followed up asking why Bitcoin hasn’t fallen further, saying "it really should be getting killed in this market."
Schiff separately argued that gold’s slide signals markets are pricing in deflation across stocks and real estate, though he expects the Federal Reserve to step in before that deflation can take hold, since it would threaten both the government’s finances and the banking system.
Rising Real Rates are Driving The Selloff
Gold fell nearly 3% Friday to $3,514 an ounce, its lowest level since September 2025 and a 15% drop for the quarter, CoinDesk reported. 
Bitcoin traded near $61,900 over the same stretch, down 28% for the quarter, and the same force is squeezing both: neither asset offers a yield that can compete with rising bond returns.
That force shows up clearly in the data:
U.S. two-year real rates have climbed above 2.40%, their highest since 2023, according to ING
10- and 30-year real yields sit at their highest levels in more than two decades
The Dollar Index has climbed to around 103.80, up more than 25% this quarter to its strongest level since April 2025
A stronger dollar and higher real yields both raise the cost of holding non-yielding assets like gold and Bitcoin, and the Fed isn’t making it easier. 
JPMorgan expects quarter-point rate hikes in January and March on top of a December increase, citing sticky inflation, even as some economists argue falling energy prices point to disinflation instead.

title: Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia
The bitcoin price slipped to near $61,500 on Friday morning, its lowest level since July, as the tech selloff spread to Asia and IBIT posted a record outflow.
This post Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia

The bitcoin price slipped to near $61,500 on Friday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a selloff in technology stocks that followed Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut spread to Asian markets and dragged bitcoin to its lowest level since July.

Bitcoin first broke below $62,000 on Thursday evening, after Thursday afternoon’s report showed it giving back a rebound toward $64,000. The bitcoin price then slid to nearly $61,200 during Asian trading before bouncing back above $61,700. Friday marks a third straight day of losses.

Asian stocks extend the AI rout

The selling started in Asia. South Korea’s Kospi slid more than 5%, with chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics down around 6%. The Korea Exchange halted program selling for five minutes after the drop, while Japan’s Nikkei fell as much as 4.85% to a seven-month low.

U.S. futures pointed lower too. Nasdaq-100 futures fell more than 1.7% and S&P 500 futures dropped 0.8%, Yahoo Finance reported. Gold futures lost 3%. The S&P 500 is pointing to a seventh straight daily decline, its longest losing streak since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

Anthropic shares fell 8% in premarket trading after closing their first session at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price. Nvidia was down about 2.4% and AMD fell nearly 7%, CNBC reported. Hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment, Reuters said.

ETF outflows and liquidations pressure the bitcoin price

Bitcoin funds are feeling the pressure. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $541.1 million in net outflows on Thursday, its largest single-day outflow since launch. That topped the previous record of $528.3 million set on Jan. 30. The fund bled $2 billion over nine straight days of outflows earlier this month.

Leveraged traders took heavy losses as the bitcoin price broke support. Bitcoin liquidations hit $712.9 million over 24 hours, with $614 million coming from long positions. Open interest in bitcoin futures fell to $18 billion from $20 billion a week ago, and funding rates flipped broadly negative as traders unwound their bets.

Traders are now watching whether the bitcoin price can hold the $60,000 area. A large pocket of long positions sits in the $60,500 to $60,900 band, just below the current price, and could come into play on a further drop. Bitcoin is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, which would be its second-longest losing streak after nine weeks of declines in 2022.

Crypto stocks slide before the bell

Crypto stocks pointed lower in premarket trading. Strategy (MSTR) traded near $83.90, down about 2.6% from Thursday’s close of $86.13, after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) slipped about 2.7% to near $106.

Bitcoin miners fell harder. IREN (IREN) dropped about 4.4%, CleanSpark (CLSK) lost about 3.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) declined about 3.4%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) was down about 3.3%. IREN has also been under pressure as investors reassess AI infrastructure stocks. Delays in bringing some of its capacity online led Microsoft to spend less with the miner than planned last quarter.

Longer-term buyers have not left entirely. Institutional investors added 49,229 BTC through U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter, lifting their holdings to a record 356,491 BTC. Swiss bank Sygnum called the current downturn the shallowest bear market for bitcoin to date, putting the drawdown at around 54% compared with declines of more than 70% in previous cycles.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,800.

This post Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

A large pocket of long positions sits in the $60,500 to $60,900 band, just below the current price, and could come into play on a further drop. Bitcoin is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, which would be its second-longest losing streak after nine weeks of declines in 2022.

Crypto stocks slide before the bell

Crypto stocks pointed lower in premarket trading. Strategy (MSTR) traded near $83.90, down about 2.6% from Thursday’s close of $86.13, after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) slipped about 2.7% to near $106.

Bitcoin miners fell harder. IREN (IREN) dropped about 4.4%, CleanSpark (CLSK) lost about 3.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) declined about 3.4%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) was down about 3.3%. IREN has also been under pressure as investors reassess AI infrastructure stocks. Delays in bringing some of its capacity online led Microsoft to spend less with the miner than planned last quarter.

Longer-term buyers have not left entirely. Institutional investors added 49,229 BTC through U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter, lifting their holdings to a record 356,491 BTC. Swiss bank Sygnum called the current downturn the shallowest bear market for bitcoin to date, putting the drawdown at around 54% compared with declines of more than 70% in previous cycles.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,800.

fullContent:
WASHINGTON—Warning Americans to keep at least 200 yards away from the livestock at all times, federal officials announced Friday that Iran had claimed credit for the hack that turned cattle into apex predators.

“Earlier this week, an Iranian hacker group connected to the Revolutionary Guard Corps broke into the Department of Agriculture’s servers, hijacked our cows’ programming, and turned them into fierce flesh-eating animals,” said agency spokesperson Delia Marchand, who admitted that the security systems of the nation’s cattle had not been updated since the early 2000s. “Cows have now ascended to the top of the food chain, killing deer, bison, and even bears. Worst of all, the group responsible has said our nation’s 85 million cows will prey upon the American people until we end the war with Iran.”

“Our experts have determined this was a complete rewriting of bovine source code,” she continued. “The cows’ eyesight and hearing have sharpened, and they can smell a drop of blood from miles away. Estimates suggest they are now hunting to eat 30 to 40 pounds of meat per day, and they have shown incredible intelligence as pack hunters: A single cow will lure a people in with a cute, calm demeanor, and then the entire herd will descend upon the prey, tearing them to pieces in seconds. Unfortunately, the hackers have locked us out of the cows programming, so we cannot undo the damage. We are looking at the world’s newest and greatest killing machines.”

Marchand added that until the federal government could lock down all remaining vulnerabilities, the nation’s fish and birds would be deactivated to make sure they weren’t similarly corrupted.

title: The Best And Worst Series Finales Of All Time
description:
A good or bad ending can make or break a TV show’s legacy. The Onion takes a look at some of the best and worst series finales ever made. BEST Reading Rainbow, “One More” (2006): The haunting final episode features host LeVar Burton looking straight into the camera and taunting children with the knowledge of […]
The post The Best And Worst Series Finales Of All Time appeared first on The Onion.
fullContent:
A good or bad ending can make or break a TV show’s legacy. The Onion takes a look at some of the best and worst series finales ever made.

BEST

Reading Rainbow, “One More” (2006): The haunting final episode features host LeVar Burton looking straight into the camera and taunting children with the knowledge of a secret 27th letter. 

Planet Earth, “Refineries” (2023): In a jarring tonal shift, the normally staid David Attenborough gives viewers step-by-step instructions on how to blow up oil refineries.

How I Met Your Mother, “Last Forever” (2014): Craig Thomas and Carter Bays thrilled fans by revealing the identity of the mother before promptly killing her off, then killing Ted Mosby, then killing their real-life families, then themselves.

Six Feet Under, “Everyone’s Waiting” (2005): Widely regarded as one of the most moving finales of all time, the drama concludes with a series of poignant flash-forwards through 2025, 2029, 2044, 2049, 2051, and 2085, showing how each character will eventually be buried alive.

The Sopranos, “Made In America” (2007): Though controversial upon initial release, the “cut to black” ending has since garnered praise for its inventive use of darkness to indicate that they didn’t film any more scenes.

Game Of Thrones, “The Iron Throne” (2019): Attention is a form of love. 

WORST

Bionic Woman, “Chiefs At Dolphins” (2007): Heavily impacted by the writers’ strike, this reboot of the ’70s sci-fi adventure series was forced to pad its episodes with NFL games.

M*A*S*H, “Goodbye, Farewell And Amen” (1983): Drawing over 105 million viewers, the two-and-a-half hour finale left factories empty, prisons unguarded, and air traffic control towers unmanned, ultimately resulting in $6 trillion damage across the U.S.

Breaking Bad, “Felina” (2013): After seven years of depicting antihero drug lord Walter White, Bryan Cranston fails to parlay the part into a role in a Marvel movie, an action franchise, a spinoff, or any other kind of career ascension that might actually bring him satisfaction.

The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson, “May 22, 1992” (1992): In his strangely vindictive send-off, the legendary Carson told America, “That’s all from me, and now you will get what you deserve.”

Pretty Little Liars, “Till Death Do Us Part” (2017): What was supposed to be the viewing party to end all viewing parties in Megan’s parents’ finished basement was ruined when Amanda brought along her volleyball friend Marissa, who spent the whole time talking over the TV, bitching about her boyfriend drama, and refusing to eat any M&M’s because she was “dieting.”

Seinfeld, “The Finale” (1998): Fans disliked this hour-long conclusion that left the show’s morally dubious protagonists arrested but unexecuted.

title: Why Are Cyber Attacks Increasing So Fast in 2026?
description:
Cyber attacks go vertical in 2026 as AI tools arm hackers, with incidents doubling since August and crypto hit hardest.
The post Why Are Cyber Attacks Increasing So Fast in 2026? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Estimated cyber attacks have more than doubled in roughly three months, Bridgewater Associates data shows. The jump began when a Chinese AI model with strong hacking skills became free to download.

Bridgewater has not proven the model caused the spike. Still, the fund now prices in a one-in-three chance of an economically destabilizing cyber attack within a year. Banks, payment firms, and crypto exchanges sit closest to that risk.

Why Did Cyber Attacks Go Vertical After August?

Capriole Investments founder Charles Edwards shared the chart on X on Nov. 20. His verdict was three words long, “truly unprecedented times.”

For nearly a decade, Bridgewater’s annualized estimate climbed slowly. It rose from about 1,500 incidents in 2017 to roughly 4,000 by mid-2026, according to the research.

Then the line turned almost straight up, reaching nearly 10,000 by November. The chart marks a single event at the turning point.

That event is the late-August release of GLM 5.3’s weights. GLM 5.3 is a coding model from Beijing-based Z.ai, formerly Zhipu AI, and anyone can download and modify it.

The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) called it “the most cyber-capable open-weight model released to date” in its assessment.

Separately, the FBI warned on Nov. 13 that hackers have used ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking framework, since at least August. Some intrusions reached privileged access in under three hours, the bureau said. However, it found DeepSeek models, not GLM, most common in attacker setups.

How Fast Are Cyber Attacks Rising Month by Month?

Check Point Research data points the same way, though less steeply. The firm tracks average weekly attacks per organization worldwide.

Growth stayed modest in the first half and even dipped below 2025 levels in March. From July, however, the yearly gap widened each month before peaking in September.

October cooled 9% from September but still ran 32% above last year. Ransomware hit a record 1,063 attacks that month, according to Check Point.

n0n, one of October’s most active ransomware groups, claimed this week’s breach of vendors serving JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard. Attackers accessed customer names and email addresses, Bloomberg reported.

Why Is Crypto Taking the Costliest Hits?

Crypto platforms absorb the largest losses. Binance lost about $6.3 billion on Oct. 29, the biggest crypto theft on record. The breach began with a fake job interview that planted malware on an engineer’s computer.

Before that single incident, DefiLlama had already logged 312 crypto hacks worth $2.4 billion in 2026. Meanwhile, Chainalysis estimates that suspected North Korean groups caused nearly 89% of this year’s hack losses. In 2021, their share was 15%.

Scams add to the toll. US victims reported $11.37 billion in crypto-related fraud losses in 2025, over half of all cybercrime losses tracked by the FBI.

Are Defenders Already Falling Behind?

Experts on BeInCrypto’s Market Intelligence Expert Council argue that AI currently favors attackers. Erica Stanford, a digital assets and AI adviser at law firm CMS and author of Crypto Wars, made that case in a recent discussion.

“It’s 100% helping criminals… anyone with no skills and not even native English or native language can now commit fraud and crimes very very easily because AI helps people do that.”

Patrick Prinz, co-founder of asset recovery firm Recoveris, agreed.

“I think it’s enabling criminals more than it helps right now the law enforcement side.”

Recovery also trails the theft itself. Binance has secured an Abu Dhabi court order over frozen funds, yet most stolen assets remain out of reach.

Prinz expects years to pass before law enforcement fields a matching response. Until then, every exchange, bank, and vendor faces attackers working at machine speed, and Bridgewater’s curve shows no sign of flattening.

The post Why Are Cyber Attacks Increasing So Fast in 2026? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: BlackRock Coinbase Prime Deposit Hits $456M in BTC, ETH
description:
It is evident BlackRock-linked wallets still move large coin stacks through Coinbase rails. Especially when Bitcoin and Ether leave the same labeled cluster on one day, the custody path matters. For BlackRock, it seems the latest BlackRock Coinbase Prime deposit just moved about 5,400 BTC and 71,597 ETH. A rather big dual-asset transfer, albeit one […]
The post BlackRock Coinbase Prime Deposit Hits $456M in BTC, ETH appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
It is evident BlackRock-linked wallets still move large coin stacks through Coinbase rails. Especially when Bitcoin and Ether leave the same labeled cluster on one day, the custody path matters. For BlackRock, it seems the latest BlackRock Coinbase Prime deposit just moved about 5,400 BTC and 71,597 ETH. A rather big dual-asset transfer, albeit one that is not exactly surprising. The firm still runs the largest US spot Bitcoin and Ether funds.

Lookonchain flagged the transfers around 12:39 UTC on November 20, 2026. The monitor put the Bitcoin leg near $331 million. The Ether leg sat near $125 million, or about $456 million combined. The post pointed readers to Arkham's BlackRock entity map. That map tracks addresses tied to the firm's ETF-linked holdings. On-chain labels can lag or miss a hop. Even so, the size and destination still give crypto ETF readers a live custody signal.

What the BlackRock Coinbase Prime Deposit Signals

This is a very worrisome development for anyone who treats every exchange deposit as a sale, to say the least. Even so, a move into Coinbase Prime was bound to draw eyes sooner or later. On the one hand, Coinbase Custody has long sat inside creation and redemption plumbing for BlackRock's funds. That includes the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) and iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA). On the other, a Prime deposit can mean inventory rebalancing. It can also mean authorized-participant settlement, or cold-to-hot handoffs that never hit the open book. The chain shows the transfer. It does not show a filled sell order.

A fair few desks still watch these rails as a rough gauge of fund demand. When coins enter Coinbase-linked wallets tied to BlackRock, traders ask two questions. Are creations warming up? Or do redemptions need coins staged for delivery? The reverse path can hint at the opposite flow. Neither reading is certain without the next day's creation and redemption prints. For now, the only hard claim is the size. About 5,400 BTC and 71,597 ETH moved into Coinbase Prime under BlackRock-linked labels.

IBIT and ETHA Stay in the Same Custody Story

It is evident the next check is not the deposit itself, to say the least. A fair few of these moves sit quiet for hours or days. On the one hand, confirmed IBIT or ETHA creations would make the transfer look like buy-side plumbing. On the other, a quiet book after a $456 million dual deposit would leave the sale scare looking thin. Even so, the dual-asset timing is the sharper tell. Bitcoin and Ether arriving together keep both funds in one custody story. That pattern is rarer than a single-coin hop.

For BlackRock, it seems the firm still trusts Coinbase Prime as a working rail for large institutional coin. The wallets Arkham marks as BlackRock remain the public map most monitors use. Until fund flow tables catch up, readers are left with the on-chain receipt. The open question is what that receipt is for. A serious custody move, though not a surprise. These rails already carry ETF-linked coin often enough.

The post BlackRock Coinbase Prime Deposit Hits $456M in BTC, ETH appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.

title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #220
description: SpaceX reusability, Leukemia vaccine (+pancreatic pill), SLAB, Tesla Powercore, Earth AI Gold + TEN Extra Doses
fullContent:
Hi friends 👋,

Happy Friday and welcome back to our 220th Weekly Dose of Optimism!

What a week to be alive. Since we spoke last Friday, GTA 6 is finally out, Anthropic is public, Starships are reusable, leukemia may not be as deadly, we may be able to live on the open seas, and… there’s just so much more. I think we might have both the highest density of great things in the Main Dose and the longest section of Extra Doses to date (there are 10 down there, including Anthropic and new Google models). Almost everything in Extra Dose would have made the top 5 even like 3 months ago.

Plus, I’ve been having a lot of fun building a new notboring.com. You can click on a bunch of the companies on the home page for little Easter Eggs, check Roundup for all of the day’s top not boring-relevant stories, and Scarce Asset Tracker for the completed and upcoming sales relevant to what I wrote in Scarce Assets. I even built a better reading experience for all of our Essays. Enjoy! And let me know what else you’d like to see, so I can tell my agents to build it.

Let’s get to it.

This Week’s Weekly Dose is brought to you by… Runway

If you want to blow your family’s mind over Thanksgiving, bring their ideas to life with Runway.

Runway is building foundational AI for how the world creates. 65M+ people use Runway to generate, edit and produce video, images and audio with 80+ top media models. You can read my essay with co-founder Anastasis Germanidis to learn more on where Runway is headed beyond video.

Nvidia, Amazon, Lionsgate, Chime, and 95%+ of the Fortune 100 are part of a growing community of teams, founders, and independent creators using Runway to make national TV spots, social ads at scale, launch videos and more.

You can also use Runway in ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Cursor, Replit and more via the Runway MCP.

Create any idea with Runway now

(1) SpaceX’s Mechazilla Catches an Orbital Starship

Humanity is one giant leap closer to being multiplanetary.

Over the weekend on Starship Flight 15, Ship 42 launched from Starbase, Texas, reached orbit, deployed a batch of Starlink satellites, spent more than 22 hours in space, survived fiery hypersonic re-entry, flipped upright, and dropped cleanly into Mechazilla’s chopsticks. The SpaceX team made one of the greatest engineering feats in human history look easy.

SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy boosters before, which was already absurd. Catching the orbital upper stage, the part that goes into orbit carrying the payload to complete a mission, was the final boss of rapid, full reusability. The final boss is dead.

While the booster is more expensive at around 70% of Starship’s cost, it is somewhat easier to reuse given that it carries the upper stage up and comes right back. Having proven that the booster is reusable, the upper stage was like 90% of the marginal cost per flight. Having to make a new one each time would leave Starship with a hard floor around $30-40M per launch, but making it reusable means that the marginal cost of launch drops to something like $2-10M per launch, or $20-100/kg versus Falcon 9’s $1,000/kg internal cost.

SpaceX still has plenty of work ahead on heat-shield durability and turnaround time before Starships are flying as repeatably as planes, of course, but the goal is to send up about two a week by the end of 2027, hundreds per year by 2029 ,and multiple per day beyond that. They’ll carry satellites and data centers and drug factories and eventually all sorts of things we’ll need to thrive in space and on other worlds.

For now, just watch the slow-motion footage above and marvel. Humans rock.

(2) Leukemia Vaccine Cuts Risk of Death by 41% in Phase 3 Trial

Video created with Runway

At this point, you know how we feel about cancer here at the Dose. Hate it.

It’s been a big year for us cancer haters, and the streak continues.

On Tuesday, SELLAS Life Sciences and Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center announced positive topline results from the pivotal Phase 3 REGAL trial of galinpepimut-S (GPS), an immunotherapeutic vaccine for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). AML is a brutal blood cancer with roughly a 33% five-year survival rate that kills around 11,500 Americans every year.

The trial followed 126 patients whose AML had relapsed, who had fought their way back into a second (or later) remission, and who weren't eligible for a stem-cell transplant. The patients were a high-risk group with very few options left.

And GPS extended their lives. Patients who received GPS alone (with no chemo alongside it) had a median overall survival of 24.0 months, compared to 14.7 months for patients on investigator's choice of best available treatment. That's more than nine extra months of life and a 41% reduction in the risk of death.

Huge. While it’s not a total cure, we seem to be entering a period in which a number of therapies are able to extend patients’ lives while researchers around the world work to find more permanent cures. Meaning, an extra nine months both nine months and a call option on much longer.

This isn’t the first promising vaccine this year. Back in Dose #207, we covered Merck and Moderna’s personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine that cut recurrence or death by 42% in Phase 3. The exciting thing about GPS isn’t custom-built from an individual tumor like that one, but an off-the-shelf peptide vaccine, which should make it faster, cheaper, and more widely available if approved. Even better, the WT1 protein shows up in a number of blood cancers and solid tumors, so GPS may be effective against more than just AML.

Say it with us… get fucked, cancer!

(2a) Pancreatic cancer pill trial saw tumours vanish

Keep saying it with us. I don’t even know what to say anymore. I got to my computer to wrap up the Dose, opened up X, and the first tweet I saw was one from the BBC saying that there’s a new pill for pancreatic cancer that shrunk tumors in one in 12 patients so completely they were undetectable in scans, and stopped tumor growth in 90% of the 61 patients.

“Experts are calling it the biggest breakthrough in pancreatic cancer treatment for decades,” the BBC reported.

This pill isn’t a cure, either, and doctors aren’t sure yet how long its effects last. But pancreatic cancer has been one of the hardest-to-drug, hardest to catch early, and therefore most deadly cancers known to mankind, and it seems that we now have a way to slow it down at the very least.

And if this year’s pace in cancer treatments is any indication, there will be more where that came from.

GET FUCKED, CANCER.

(3) Palmer Luckey Reveals SLAB, a 1,000-Year Floating Seastead

Well, here’s a happy challenge we might have to deal with. If people live a lot longer, where are we going to but them all?

Bah gaw that’s Palmer Luckey’s music!

Fresh off announcing Warhound and a drumbeat of positive Anduril announcements, Luckey announced on X (to preempt a journalist working on the story) that he’s “developing a seastead called SLAB with a 1,000 year design life.”

To get ahead of people thinking he might just be another guy doing an ocean data center thing (this is “way cooler” than that, Palmer said that he’s actually been privately funding and building SLAB since selling Oculus to Facebook for $2 billion in 2014. He and some friends capitalized it at a $1 billion valuation, and put more money in recently.

The idea is that SLAB will be a massive off-shore floating industrial platform engineered to last a thousand years that’s meant to be cheaper than land while operating outside the regulatory morass that chokes American heavy industry. On SLAB, future Palmers may build factories for metal processing, desalination, oil refining, chemical engineering, and frontier medical research and treatment.

Thousand Year Luckey Empire.

(4) Tesla Unveils Powercore, a 7.4 MW Solid-State Transformer

Tesla announced that it’s doing solid state transformers with its new Powercore.

Ho hum. Another week, another huge chunk of the capability stack that eliminates a big bottleneck and also plays really well with the other pieces of the stack from The Musk Companies. Just look at how much of the future this man controls:

We’ve talked about SSTs in the context of Heron Power, founded by ex-Tesla SVP of Powertrain and Energy Engineering, Drew Baglino many times, in Dose #181, Dose #183, Dose #187, and Thank God for Data Centers. We are fans of both Drew and of SSTs, for their ability to speed up and cost down data center construction today and potentially help stabilize the grid in the future.

I think both Heron and Tesla will do well here. There is a ton of demand, and as I wrote in the America Spins on Westmag:

In the Electric Era, maintaining design leadership without manufacturing leadership is not a coherent strategic position, and one that gets less coherent the better you believe AI will get.

Elon has solved this by building practically everything inside of his own companies. There is a parallel American ecosystem emerging to serve the growing number of electric companies not in the Elonverse.

A few years ago, we barely had one modern industrial base. Now we have two. 🇺🇸

(5) Earth AI Uncovers a 3km Copper-Gold-Platinum System

If those two parallel electric universes do even one-tenth of what they’re planning to do, we’re going to need a lot of metal. Challenge is: the world spends something like $14 billion searching for new mineral deposits, but major discoveries have dropped ~70% over the past decade. We’ve already pulled out the easy stuff, and it’s going to take new technology to get at the harder stuff economically.

Luckily, as you may know, we are in a golden age of technology, and our friends and not boring capital portfolio company Earth AI are using it to find metals.. This week, the company announced that its Alpheus AI model found a continuous copper, gold, and platinum-group metals system stretching more than 3 kilometers at the Fontenoy/Meridian project in New South Wales, Australia. There’s some Tungsten in there too. Roman showed me one of the rocks - the Tungsten shows up as black spots and is easy to mistake for nothing.

Explorers actually drilled the site back in 1969 and again in 1997, but they thought it was just some scattered pockets that wouldn’t have been economical to mind. Back in January, Earth AI turned its models on the old data, and the models recognized that they weren’t looking at discontinuous “black smoker” pockets; they predicted that it was actually a massive magma-filled fault line.

Five weeks later, Earth AI started drilling (it owns its own rigs and labs, so it didn’t have to wait for slow and expensive contractors; vertical integration ftw). It’s drilled 35 holes and traced mineralization from 30m to 478m deep across the 3km seam, with hints that it might actually be 8km long.

As we covered in our Deep Dive on Earth AI, discovery is just the first step in a long process towards getting metal out of the ground, but with its rigs, it’s moving towards feasibility more quickly than other explorers traditionally could.

I think the company has the potential to be one of the world’s most beautiful businesses as these discoveries prove out, sell off, and turn into cash which buys more rigs and allows Earth AI to prove out the other 4,500 targets on its list. This week’s news is a golden step in the right direction.

title: Trump can finally deliver the immigration bargain Reagan was promised
description: Attorney Mehek Cooke argues that Trump can fix Reagan's failed 1986 amnesty bargain by mandating E-Verify and codifying border security before any legal relief expands.
fullContent:
Washington broke immigration and now offers America two politically convenient but false extremes: deport everyone or grant blanket amnesty. This choice prevents us from solving a problem intentionally created by decades of government failure, weak enforcement and an open invitation to abuse our laws.

President Ronald Reagan’s 1986 immigration bargain granted legal status to millions of illegal immigrants while Washington’s enforcement commitment proved temporary and inadequate. President Donald Trump can reverse that historic imbalance by making enforcement permanent and offering compassion through the rule of law. Trump has opened negotiations with Democrats while keeping blanket amnesty off the table. His approach prioritizes the removal of criminals, including murderers, rapists and drug dealers, while evaluating long-term residents with clean records and American families individually under the law.

Democrats are responding to Trump’s invitation with a nonstarter: The Protect Our Neighbors Act would allow final removal orders to magically expire after 10 years and create a pathway to permanent residency for certain illegal immigrants. Due process has already produced those final orders, yet Democrats would create a perverse incentive for illegal immigrants to evade removal until they reach the 10-year mark and qualify for permanent residency. This is the definition of insanity: rewarding the failure to enforce the law and calling it immigration reform.

WHITE HOUSE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER TRUMP ANGERS BASE BY FLOATING ILLEGAL ALIEN DEAL WITH DEMS

History reveals why this is the wrong starting point. Reagan’s 1986 immigration law granted legal status to nearly 2.7 million people while creating employer sanctions and border funding. However, employers were considered compliant if the I-9 documents appeared genuine. The GAO found that 39% of unauthorized workers identified in five major cities used or were suspected of using fraudulent documents, and investigators often could not establish that the employer had the knowledge required for sanctions.

By the 1990s, a Congressional Research Service analysis found that the unauthorized population exceeded its pre-IRCA level. Border enforcement followed the same pattern because legalization was not conditioned on control. Despite increased funding, the GAO found unfilled positions, reduced agent time on border control and failing equipment that left high-traffic areas vulnerable to illegal entry and drug smuggling and unpatrolled. The blunt truth is that compassion without enforceable security became an open invitation to repeat the crisis.\

President Trump holds a unique position of strength as he confronts immigration reform because he first enforced the law. In fiscal year 2026, southwest border apprehensions fell approximately 95% below the Biden-era annual average, and Border Patrol completed its first fiscal year with zero releases into the United States. Trump proved that existing law could secure the border when a president has the will to enforce it. For permanent security, Congress must codify his border policies, mandate nationwide E-Verify, impose serious penalties on employers who knowingly hire and exploit illegal labor and limit future presidents’ ability to unilaterally dismantle these protections.

To prevent another failure, any future immigration agreement must include benchmarks: publicly reported removals, zero Border Patrol releases and a fully operational nationwide employment-verification system maintained for at least one year before legal relief expands. Enforcement must serve as a condition for future relief.

TRUMP'S IMMIGRATION OLIVE BRANCH THREATENS TO OPEN PANDORA'S BOX AS EXPERTS WARN OF FAR-REACHING FALLOUT

Rejecting blanket amnesty does not require treating every illegal immigrant alike. A cartel member and a father who entered illegally 15 years ago, paid taxes, raised American children and has no criminal record present fundamentally different cases. To be clear, neither entered lawfully, and good behavior alone cannot erase that violation, but it should matter when a judge reviews the case. Existing law permits certain illegal immigrants in removal proceedings to seek cancellation of removal after 10 years of continuous presence, good moral character, no disqualifying criminal convictions and proof that removal would cause exceptional and extremely unusual hardship to a U.S.-citizen or lawful-permanent-resident spouse, parent or child. An immigration judge retains discretion, and Congress caps most grants at 4,000 annually, proving that individualized relief is not blanket amnesty.

FORMER BORDER PATROL CHIEF RECALLS BIDEN MIGRANT SURGE CHAOS AS TRUMP CRACKDOWN DELIVERS HISTORIC TURNAROUND

Congress should fund additional immigration judges to reduce the case backlog and deliver timely decisions. It should also create a streamlined federal review process, so each judge receives a verified case file containing the evidence necessary to evaluate every legal requirement. The solution is not weaker standards, but faster decisions and consistent enforcement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Washington failed Reagan by trading permanent legal status for temporary enforcement promises. President Trump can now apply Reagan’s own standard: Trust, but verify. Congress must permanently codify border security to ensure no future president can simply erase it with the stroke of a pen.

President Trump can finally deliver the bargain Reagan deserved: a secure border, case-by-case compassion under the law and permanent protection for the American people.

title: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $62K: What Should You Do?
description:
Bitcoin price falls below $62K, ETF outflows hit $582M, and liquidations mount. Can BTC defend $60K, or is another crash toward $53K coming?
The post Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $62K: What Should You Do? appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
Bitcoin price has fallen below $62,000 for the first time since early July, extending a brutal November selloff as institutional investors pull billions from the market. BTC touched $61,270 just now, before recovering slightly to trade around $61,700.

Bitcoin price has now lost more than 10% over seven days, with selling pressure spreading across equities, precious metals and other risk assets. Yesterday’s $582.2 million outflow from US spot Bitcoin ETFs added another blow, bringing November withdrawals close to $3.5 billion.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest single-day outflow since launching. The same session saw $727 million in crypto liquidations, with bullish traders absorbing most of the damage.

Institutional demand is weakening, leveraged buyers are being forced out, and the Federal Reserve’s increasingly hawkish outlook is making speculative assets less attractive.

Bitcoin is now approaching $60,000, a level that could determine if the correction finds a floor or develops into something uglier.

Xrp (XRP)
24h7d30d1yAll time

Bitcoin ETF Exodus and $727M Liquidations Put Bulls on the Defensive

The ETF withdrawals are arguably the biggest concern for Bitcoin holders right now. Spot Bitcoin ETFs became an important source of institutional demand after launching in January 2024. Their buying helped absorb available supply and gave traditional investors a regulated route into the market.

That demand is now moving in the opposite direction. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $1.1 billion this week alone. November’s cumulative withdrawals have approached $3.5 billion.

The pressure extends beyond ETFs. Rising Treasury yields and expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase in December have encouraged investors to reduce exposure to assets that offer no regular income.

Meanwhile, derivatives traders are taking heavy losses. CoinGlass data showed more than $700 million in liquidations across crypto markets over 24 hours. Long positions accounted for 86% of the total.

Bitcoin itself recorded nearly $202 million in liquidations, with bullish traders suffering the majority of forced closures.

This creates a difficult environment for buyers. Falling prices trigger liquidations, which create additional selling pressure and push prices lower. The reduction in open interest also suggests excessive leverage is being flushed from the market.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Bitcoin Price Prediction: $60K Breakdown or Relief Rally?

The immediate battle is around $60,000. Bitcoin needs to reclaim $62,000 and establish support above it before bulls can confidently argue that the latest breakdown was temporary.

There are three possible scenarios:

Scenario 1: Bitcoin loses $60K and heads toward $58K or $53K.

This is the bearish outcome. A decisive break below $60,000 could trigger another wave of stop-loss orders and leveraged liquidations.

The next downside area sits around $58,000, while more aggressive technical projections point toward $53,700.

The daily chart offers little encouragement for bulls. Bitcoin trades below its major moving averages, while bearish momentum continues to dominate. A sustained recovery in ETF flows would become increasingly important to prevent further deterioration.

Scenario 2: Bitcoin stabilizes between $60K and $62K.

This would give buyers time to absorb available supply without immediately reversing the entire November decline.

The liquidation wave has already removed considerable leverage from the market. If ETF withdrawals begin slowing, Bitcoin could establish a trading range before attempting another recovery.

But sideways trading alone would not confirm a bottom. Buyers need to demonstrate that they can defend support through multiple sessions.

Scenario 3: Bitcoin reclaims $62K and launches a relief rally.

A recovery above $62,000 would provide the first meaningful sign that sellers are losing control. A move toward $65,000 would then become possible, followed by resistance around $68,000.

Consistent ETF inflows, improving market sentiment, and a weaker dollar would strengthen this scenario. Without those developments, any rebound risks becoming another opportunity for sellers to exit.

Should Bitcoin Holders Sell, Hold or Buy the Dip?

For existing holders, the decision depends heavily on their entry price, investment horizon, and exposure. Long-term holders who bought substantially below current prices have more room to withstand volatility. Selling simply because Bitcoin crossed a psychological threshold risks locking in profits or losses without knowing whether the broader investment thesis has changed.

However, investors holding leveraged positions face a different problem. Falling prices can trigger forced liquidations regardless of their long-term convictions. Reducing leverage and protecting available capital should take priority over waiting for a rebound.

For buyers, the temptation to buy the dip is understandable. Bitcoin is considerably cheaper than it was just weeks ago, but cheaper does not automatically mean undervalued.

Buying in stages rather than committing an entire allocation around $61,000 offers more flexibility if the market tests $58,000 or even $53,700.

Bitcoin price remains vulnerable to another leg down. The $60,000 level is no longer just a psychological milestone. It is where the next major battle between buyers and sellers.

title: Monero Price Likely to Offer Another Selling Opportunity as XMR1 Holders Lose 99%
description: A wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid lost 99% in minutes. Native XMR is separate but trades below its 200-day average, with resistance near $500.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • A Wagyu-issued wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid lost about 99% of its value in roughly half an hour.
  • Native XMR is a separate asset, yet it now trades below both its 50-day and 200-day averages.
  • The nearest ceiling sits near $500, and support lies far below it.

Holders of XMR1, a wrapped Monero token issued by Wagyu, were wiped out on Hyperliquid after the deployer account moved most of the supply to a fresh wallet and sold. Blockchain sleuths flagged the move as suspected theft.

Native Monero held up, though the coin was already sliding and now sits on fragile ground. Traders want to know whether any bounce can hold, or whether it just hands sellers a better exit.

Wrapped Monero Token XMR1 Collapses 99% on Hyperliquid

A wrapped Monero token issued by Wagyu lost almost all of its value on Hyperliquid on Nov 20, 2026. The token, XMR1, slid from about $494 to below $1 in roughly half an hour. That was a drop of 99.8%.

On-chain records show the token's deployer account sent 5.2 million XMR1 to a newly created wallet. The coins moved in three transfers between 04:46 and 05:16 UTC: two of 100,000 and one of 5,000,000. Before the moves, the deployer controlled 93% of supply.

The seller then dumped into thin liquidity. Bitquery data show 363,804 tokens sold for $13.5 million to 388 buyers. A few large buyers accounted for most of the proceeds. About 4.83 million tokens stayed in the wallet.

Next, the proceeds went into ETH through CoW Protocol on Arbitrum, with $13.22 million in USDC swapped. The funds were then bridged out via Socket, Mayan and Stargate. Roughly 4,836 ETH landed in a fresh wallet.

Lookonchain flagged the address, and Scam Sniffer called it suspected theft. Nobody yet knows whether this was a hack or authorized use, since the transfers needed the deployer's main key. That gap raises hard questions about Wagyu's wallet security and what actually backs XMR1.

Spot XMR, a separate asset, traded near $463.86 that day, while Hyperliquid XMR futures sat near $482.

Monero Slips Under Both Averages as Sellers Extend a Monthly Slide

Monero (XMR) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

XMR changed hands near $461 at last check, down about 7% over the past 24 hours.

The bigger problem is where price sits relative to its trend lines. A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the general direction over a set period. XMR trades well below its 50-day average near $551, which now acts as a ceiling. It also slipped just under its 200-day average, around $474, a line many traders treat as the boundary between a healthy and a broken trend.

Losing both averages at once is a bearish setup. It means short-term and long-term buyers are now holding at a loss.

The slide started well before the XMR1 incident. Monero is down about 17% over the past week and roughly 23% over the past month. Sellers were already in control when the wrapped token collapsed.

Wider market weakness adds to the strain. Bitcoin fell about 3.9% to near $61,473, and Ether dropped roughly 4.4% to around $1,733. When the two largest coins retreat, smaller assets like XMR rarely find buyers on their own.

Momentum Nears Exhaustion Without Turning

The daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 31. That reading is weak and close to the oversold line at 30. It has not crossed it, though, so there is no clear signal that selling has run its course.

A dip below 30 would show sellers are tiring, but it would not mark a bottom on its own.

Other gauges point the same way. The MACD, which tracks shifts in momentum, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, downside momentum is still building rather than fading.

Trend strength readings also confirm a real trend, and sellers are leading it. Short bounces in this setup often attract fresh selling instead of new buyers.

Why $500 Caps Any Relief Rally

The first real ceiling sits near $500, the nearest resistance on the daily chart. XMR traded there before this week's drop. Buyers who got in there now have a chance to exit near breakeven, so any bounce into that zone is likely to meet supply.

A close above that level would ease some pressure. Bulls would then need to clear $522 to show the slide has paused. Until both levels fall, rallies look like chances to sell.

The downside picture is more worrying. Nearest support sits far lower, around $169, with the next floor near $145. That leaves a wide gap with few clear levels to slow a decline.

If the 200-day area gives way for good, price could fall quickly through that empty space.

Two Paths for XMR Over the Next Three Days

XMR's direction hinges on how price reacts at first resistance.

  • Bullish: A daily close above first resistance would open a move toward the next barrier overhead. That would show buyers absorbing the supply left from before this week's drop. The setup fails if price slips back under the 200-day average.
  • Bearish: A rejection at first resistance keeps sellers in charge and pushes price deeper below the 200-day line. With support far below, losses could build quickly. A close above the next barrier would cancel this view.

Rallies Remain Selling Opportunities for Now

The trend still favors sellers. Bounces toward resistance look like exits for now. Trimming exposure there makes more sense than chasing a turn.

Risk cuts both ways. The gap down to support is wide, so a breakdown could move fast. Momentum near oversold territory can also spark sharp short squeezes that punish late sellers.

The post XRP Supply Shortage on Binance Tops July Levels, CryptoQuant Analyst Says appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
US spot XRP (XRP) ETFs have gone 15 straight trading days without an inflow, their longest drought since launch. Meanwhile, XRP supply on Binance has tightened past its July level.

Thin exchange supply can limit selling pressure. However, it only supports prices when buyers show up. That puts the spotlight on ETF investors, who have stayed away since late October.

October 29 Was the Last Day XRP ETFs Took In Money

The funds last drew a net inflow of $8.43 million on October 29, SoSoValue data shows. Since then, they have shed $26.29 million. The previous longest dry spell lasted 8 trading days, from March 5 to 16.

The outflows now span 3 straight weeks. The funds lost $6.14 million on November 17 alone. That followed $19.13 million in withdrawals during the week ending November 13, an 8-month weekly high.

Total net assets slid to $1.08 billion by November 19, down from $1.77 billion on September 25.

Still, cumulative net inflows since launch stand near $1.78 billion. Existing holders have largely stayed, while new money has paused.

On Binance, the picture looks different. CryptoQuant’s Supply Shortage Index tracks how scarce XRP is on the exchange.

The index reached 2.4 on November 19, above its July 6 reading of 2.09, analyst Amr Taha noted. Readings above 2 point to severe tightness.

XRP whales have been pulling coins off the exchange too. They withdrew over $127 million net between November 10 and 16, analyst Darkfost reported.

However, Darkfost added that part of that flow may be internal Binance transfers. He saw similar moves after the exchange’s $6.3 billion hack, when it rebuilt reserves.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

Can Tight Supply Lift the XRP Price Without ETF Buyers?

XRP price stood at $0.96581 at press time, according to BeInCrypto Markets data. The token has lost 3.61% over the past week.

Risk-adjusted returns also look weak. XRP’s 30-day Sharpe ratio sits near -0.41. A negative reading means its recent returns have fallen short of the risk its price swings carry.

XRP also trades below its 200-day moving average, which sits near $1.26. Taha said tighter supply could help a recovery if buyers return. On its own, though, it does not confirm a reversal.

Arab Chain pointed to improving Sharpe readings and a reclaim of key technical levels as the signals to watch.

A return of XRP ETF inflows would be the first sign that demand is meeting Binance’s thin supply.
