title: Pi Network (PI) Price Collapse, Ripple (XRP) Predictions, and More: Bits Recap Nov 20
description: A closer look at the recent performance of PI, XRP, and ADA.
fullContent:
Despite recent ecosystem updates, Pi Network’s PI continues to plunge and has dropped to a new historic low.

Ripple’s XRP has also headed south and, according to some analysts, is at risk of a further brutal crash. For its part, Cardano (ADA) lost a key psychological barrier, while the latest news surrounding the project has been far from encouraging.

PI’s New Bottom

The popular altcoin has plummeted nearly 80% over the past week, and its market capitalization has shrunk to $580 million (per CoinGecko), making it the 91st-biggest cryptocurrency. PI lost 10% of its valuation in the last day alone and currently trades just north of $0.05, the lowest level in its history.

The token’s renewed pullback coincides with a sell-off across the broader crypto market, where Bitcoin (BTC) slipped below $62,000, while Ethereum (ETH) lost $1,800.

PI’s red day also comes right after the conclusion of Pi Network’s Ecosystem Summit, an online event held between November 17 and November 19. The team had previously detailed the summit’s agenda and focus:

“Three days of developer platform announcements, technical demonstrations, developer conversations, and app showcases, featuring new opportunities to build on Pi.”

Several hours ago, the Core Team shed more light on the event’s final day, which includes a special hackathon offering a 200,000 USDT prize pool.

“Build apps for Pi’s ecosystem of 60+ million engaged users using AI coding agents, Pi’s Developer Console, and tools released at this Ecosystem Summit. Or bring self-hosted applications to SoloHost. Pi Foundation has also allocated up to 20 million Pi in the App Growth Initiative to provide marketing support to help eligible apps attract and engage users,” the announcement reads.

XRP Bleeds Out

The cryptocurrency correction hasn’t been kind to Ripple’s cross-border token, too, which plunged below the $1 psychological mark. As of press time, it trades near $0.95, down 7% on a weekly basis.

Ali Martinez recently suggested that a large ascending triangle has been developing on XRP’s weekly chart since 2017. He noted that the asset is down over 40% since its October high of $1.55, claiming this structure signals that the pullback could extend toward the rising trendline at around $0.78.

“That’s where I would expect buyers to step in. If $0.78 holds, XRP could begin a much larger recovery toward the triangle’s horizontal resistance around $3.50,” he added.

For their part, ChartNerd claimed the asset’s next expansion is taking shape as the price approaches a six-year support floor for a third retest.

“Historically, 85-95% corrections have established the retests preceding major breakouts. Hold the line, structure confirms,” the analyst concluded.

How’s ADA Doing?

Cardano’s native token tumbled by roughly 13% on a weekly scale, currently trading under $0.15. Despite the downtrend, Sjuul | AltCryptoGems thinks it remains above a key support level.

“I’m just not sure that the unswept low just below the current price is that safe. For a meaningful reversal, we probably need to hunt the liquidity there first,” he added.

Meanwhile, Cardano’s team revealed that DJED, the network’s overcollateralized stablecoin, and the reserve token SHEN will be shut down on December 31, 2026. To learn about the latest ecosystem developments, check out our dedicated article here.

title: ETH May Slide to $1,000 if $1,500 Breaks on a Higher Timeframe Close, CryptoPatel Warns
description: Ethereum sits deeply oversold as ETF outflows and exchange inflows build. Analyst CryptoPatel says a close below $1,500 could open a slide toward $1,000.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Fresh coins are flowing onto exchanges while spot Ethereum ETFs log a seventh straight week of outflows.
  • Ether looks deeply oversold on the daily chart, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • Analyst CryptoPatel says a higher-timeframe close below $1,500 could open a much deeper slide.

Ethereum faces a test of nerve as on-chain data show coins moving back to exchanges and fund investors keep pulling money out. Analyst CryptoPatel warned that a break of one key level could send ETH sharply lower.

The warning lands after a bruising month for the second-largest crypto asset. Oversold readings hint at a possible bounce, yet buyers have stayed quiet.

Exchange Inflows and ETF Exits Put $1,500 in Focus

Ethereum is drawing fresh coins onto exchanges as its price slides. CryptoQuant data show exchange reserves fell to about 14.43 million ETH on Nov 16. They jumped by roughly 140,000 ETH the next day and have held near 14.57 million since.

Binance logged a net inflow of 17,485 ETH during the decline. Coins moving to an exchange often signal plans to sell, though an inflow alone does not prove a sale.

Fund flows point the same way. Spot Ethereum ETFs lost about $398.9 million in the week ending Nov 13, their seventh straight week of outflows. Santiment offered the lone counter signal, tracking a one-day net outflow of 4,186 stETH from exchanges. That was the largest since May 30.

Analyst CryptoPatel places ETH near the top of a $1,646 to $1,744 zone. He calls $1,500 the key test and warns that a higher-timeframe close below it could expose $1,000. A move above $2,807 would be the first sign of a broader bullish shift, he said. Merlijn The Trader sees $1,575 as the next potential stop.

ETH Trades Far Beneath Both Averages After a 29% Month

Ethereum (ETH) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Ether traded near $1,740 on the latest data, unchanged over the past day. The calm session follows a rough stretch. ETH lost about 14% over the week and roughly 29% over the past month.

That monthly drop leaves the token near the bottom of its 30-day range. Buyers who stepped in during the past few weeks are now holding losses. That can add supply on any rebound, as traders look to exit near their entry price.

Moving averages show the depth of the damage. A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the underlying trend. The 50-day average sits near $2,190. The 200-day average is higher, around $2,260. ETH trades well beneath both, so each line now acts as a ceiling overhead.

The 50-day line has slipped below the 200-day line. That means the recent trend is weaker than the longer one, a pattern traders read as a sign of lasting pressure. The wide gap between price and both lines shows how quickly the selling has run.

A session without new losses suggests sellers paused after a heavy week. A single quiet day does not make a reversal, though. ETH would need to string together higher closes before the chart shows real repair.

Oversold Readings Have Not Stopped the Sellers

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 22 on the daily chart. Any reading below 30 counts as oversold. It means sellers have pushed the price down faster than usual, and markets in that state often stage short relief bounces.

An oversold reading alone gives no buy signal. Momentum still points down on the MACD. Sellers have not yet lost their grip on the daily trend.

Trend strength readings back that up. They show a real trend in place, and sellers are the ones driving it. In strong downtrends, RSI can stay pinned in oversold territory for days or even weeks.

A bounce would carry more weight if momentum turned higher while the price stopped setting fresh lows.

Why $2,170 Matters More Than Any Bounce

Nearest resistance sits near $2,170, just under the 50-day line. A daily close above it would be the first real repair on the chart. It would put ETH back above a ceiling sellers have defended through the slide. The next barrier waits near $2,280, close to the 200-day average.

The downside map looks thinner. Chart support does not appear until about $1,200, and no level is marked in between. That gap makes CryptoPatel's key test the practical floor for now. Analysts flag a broad $1,500 to $1,800 band as possible support. Convincing buyers have not shown up there yet.

Traders would first want to see ETH recover around $1,900. That recovery would show demand returning before price tests the heavier resistance overhead.

Two Roads From the Bottom of the Range

ETH now sits between a crowded ceiling and a thin floor, and the next decisive move sets the path.

  • Bullish: An oversold relief rally that clears the reassuring level analysts flagged would open a run at nearest resistance, just under the 50-day line. A slide back under Merlijn The Trader's next stop would cancel that setup.
  • Bearish: Losing Merlijn's stop would bring CryptoPatel's floor into play, with the chart's lone support level waiting below. A daily close back above the reassuring level would invalidate this case.

Oversold but Not Yet Bought

ETH looks stretched enough for a bounce. The trend still belongs to sellers until the price reclaims resistance under the 50-day line.

The bigger risk sits in the flows. If ETF exits and exchange inflows keep building, a break of that floor could turn into the deeper slide CryptoPatel warned about.

title: Sui Price Outlook for December: One Level Remains Critical After Hashi Goes Live
description: Hashi is live on Sui, letting Bitcoin holders borrow USDC. SUI still trades below key averages, and support near $0.56 now decides December's floor.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • Hashi is now live on Sui mainnet, letting Bitcoin holders borrow USDC without selling their BTC.
  • SUI still trades below both key moving averages, and momentum keeps pointing lower.
  • One support level now decides whether buyers have any floor left in December.

Bitcoin holders can now borrow USDC against their coins on Sui. The Hashi protocol went live on mainnet this week, opening a door to the largest pool of capital in crypto.

The launch lands at an awkward moment for SUI. Sellers have controlled the token for a month, and the new product has not changed that. Traders now want to know whether the chart can hold long enough for Hashi demand to show up.

Why Is Sui Falling Even After Hashi Went Live?

Sui is falling because a month of steady selling has outweighed the Hashi launch, at least for now. The new Bitcoin lending product has not turned the chart.

On Wednesday the token traded near $0.69, down about 3% in a day. The token has lost roughly 15% over the past week and about 34% over the past month. Sellers have kept control through the whole stretch.

New infrastructure rarely moves price on launch day. Hashi needs Bitcoin holders to deposit BTC, take loans and generate fees before it shows up in network activity. That process takes weeks or months.

Price works on a shorter clock. Traders are reacting to broader selling today, so the long-term story and the daily tape point in different directions.

What Is Hashi and Who Can Use It on Sui?

Hashi is a lending tool on Sui that lets anyone holding Bitcoin borrow USDC, a dollar-pegged stablecoin, without selling their BTC. The protocol runs on Sui mainnet as Bitcoin finance infrastructure for the network.

The appeal is simple. A Bitcoin holder can unlock cash for spending or trading while keeping exposure to BTC. The coins serve as collateral, and the loan comes out in stablecoins.

For Sui, the upside lies in who might show up. Bitcoin is the largest pool of capital in crypto, and most of it sits idle. If a slice of it moves onto Sui as collateral, the network could gain liquidity, users and fee income.

That potential remains untested. The project has not disclosed deposit figures, loan volumes or the names of the people behind it.

How Low Can SUI Go in December?

Sui (SUI) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

SUI trades below its 50-day average near $0.87. It also sits under its 200-day average near $0.94. Both lines now act as ceilings overhead. Trend strength readings confirm a real downtrend, and sellers are the ones driving it.

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits at 31. That puts the token close to oversold territory, where selling often starts to tire. Momentum is still pointing down, though, so the chart shows no reversal signal yet.

The key floor sits near $0.56, the green line on the daily chart. The data shows no clear support below it. A break under that level would leave buyers without an obvious place to step in.

Any bounce faces resistance first near $0.80. Above that, sellers are likely waiting around $0.95, close to the 200-day line. SUI would need to clear both before the Hashi story can show up in price.

What Should SUI Traders Watch This Week?

Three things will tell traders whether the Hashi news can start to matter.

  • The green support line. A close below it would open the way to further losses.
  • The first red resistance line. A move back above it would be the first sign that sellers are tiring.
  • Early Hashi usage. Rising BTC deposits and USDC loans would show real demand reaching Sui.

title: Ali Martinez Sees a Possible DOGE Rebound From $0.054, the Level Behind a 760% Rally
description: Analyst Ali Martinez says Dogecoin is back at the $0.054 support that launched two big rallies. Here is what the chart shows and what would confirm a rebound.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • Ali Martinez says Dogecoin is back at a support zone that has launched two major rallies since 2022.
  • Daily momentum looks oversold, yet sellers still control the trend on both short and long time frames.
  • Everything hinges on whether buyers can defend the floor on a closing basis.

Dogecoin has slid back to a price zone that crypto analyst Ali Martinez calls one of its most important floors. He said a successful defense could set up another sharp rebound.

The call follows a bruising November for meme coins, with mid-size holders buying and the largest whales selling. Will history repeat at this floor, or will a third test finally break it?

Martinez Points to the Floor That Launched Two Big Rallies

Crypto analyst Ali Martinez says Dogecoin has returned to the $0.054 zone, a level that has served as major support since 2022. He pointed to two earlier tests of that floor. DOGE rallied 184% after the November 2022 test. The June 2023 test sparked a gain of about 760%.

"If this level holds once again, we could see another significant rebound from here," Martinez said.

The setup comes after a rough month. DOGE has dropped more than 25% in November, moving lower alongside Shiba Inu.

On-chain data from Santiment shows a split among holders. Mid-size wallets added 440 million DOGE between Sept. 29 and Nov. 17. Larger whales trimmed about 20 million DOGE over the same stretch.

Analyst Davie Satoshi went further. He compared the current correction to the 2018 to 2020 consolidation that came before a rally of more than 36,000%. That comparison is speculative, and past cycles offer no guarantee of a repeat.

Both Key Averages Now Sit Far Overhead

Dogecoin (DOGE) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

DOGE trades near $0.057, flat over the past 24 hours. The quiet day follows a heavy stretch. The coin is down about 14% over the past week and roughly 30% over the past month.

Both of the main moving averages sit well above the current price. A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the broader direction. The 50-day average, which tracks the recent trend, stands near $0.073. The 200-day average, a gauge of the longer trend, sits around $0.086.

Price below both lines confirms a downtrend on two time frames. Those averages now act as ceilings. Any rally would likely meet sellers well before it reached either one.

The monthly slide has pushed DOGE to the low end of its recent range. That leaves the price only a few fractions of a cent above the floor Martinez flagged. The gap is small enough that one more bad week could put his support to the test.

Earlier in November, the chart broke down. DOGE slipped out of a descending channel and lost support near $0.059. That level had held up the price during the first leg down. Once it gave way, sellers met little resistance on the way toward Martinez's zone.

Oversold Readings Have Not Yet Slowed the Sellers

The daily RSI sits near 28. RSI is a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, and readings below 30 count as oversold. That means sellers have pushed the price down hard and fast, perhaps faster than the news justifies.

Oversold conditions often come before relief bounces. They do not guarantee one. In a strong downtrend, RSI can stay pinned at low levels for weeks while the price keeps sliding.

Other gauges show that risk. The MACD, a tool that tracks shifts in momentum, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings also confirm a real trend, and sellers lead it.

Together, these signals describe a stretched market that has yet to turn.

$0.072 Stands Between DOGE and a Real Recovery

The live data shows no confirmed support below the current price. That leaves Martinez's zone as the practical floor. Buyers have to defend it on their own, with no chart level underneath to catch a slip.

Resistance sits much higher. The first barrier stands near $0.072, close to where the 50-day average now runs. A close above it would undo the channel break from earlier this month. It would also tell traders that buyers had finally taken back control of the short-term trend.

The next hurdle sits around $0.078. Clearing that level would put DOGE above the 50-day line and give the rebound case some real weight.

Below the floor, the path looks shorter. Analysts have discussed a move toward $0.04 if Martinez's floor gives way. A break there would erase the support that launched both earlier rallies.

What Would Confirm or Break the Bounce Case

  • Bullish: If buyers defend the floor and reclaim the broken channel support from earlier this month, the path opens toward first resistance near the 50-day line. A close below Martinez's zone would cancel this setup.
  • Bearish: A daily close beneath Martinez's floor would put the lower target analysts discussed in play. A recovery back above the old channel support would invalidate that view and suggest the sell-off has run its course.

History Favors Buyers Only If the Floor Holds

Martinez's floor offers traders a clear line to lean on, and two past rallies give the rebound case some history. The trend still belongs to sellers, though, and nothing on the chart has turned yet.

Support tends to weaken with each retest. If the largest whales keep trimming their holdings, a third visit to the zone could crack instead of bounce.

title: BTC Funds Draw a Net $4B in Q3, Ending Nine Months of Institutional Selling
description: Institutions bought a net $4 billion of bitcoin funds in Q3, ending nine months of selling. BTC now trades near $62,000 with key support at $59,000.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Institutional investors turned net buyers of bitcoin funds in the third quarter after three straight quarters of selling.
  • The daily chart shows bitcoin deeply oversold, yet sellers still control momentum.
  • One nearby support level now stands between bitcoin and open air below.

Big investors bought a net $4 billion of bitcoin funds in the third quarter. The buying ended nine months of steady selling by the same group.

The timing makes the figure awkward for bulls. Bitcoin has slid hard since the quarter closed, and that summer demand has not stopped the drop. Traders now want to know whether those buyers will step back in at lower prices.

Institutions Return With $4 Billion After Nine Months Away

The quarterly inflow marks a clear change in behavior. Large holders had been net sellers for the previous nine months, steadily trimming their exposure through the first half of the year.

The reversal suggests professional money saw value at summer prices. Funds that had been heading for the exit started adding again. For a market that leans on big buyers to absorb supply, that shift carries weight.

Details remain thin. Only the headline figures from the report are available, with no breakdown by fund, issuer or investor type. Readers should treat the total as a broad snapshot of direction.

Timing matters too, since the data covers July through September. It says nothing about how institutions have behaved during the steep November sell-off, which began weeks after the quarter closed.

Bitcoin Trades Far Beneath a Shared $75K Average

Bitcoin (BTC) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Bitcoin traded near $62,000 on Thursday, well below the levels that defined its recent trend. Both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages now sit around $75,000. A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the typical price over a set period. When price trades below it, that average tends to act as a ceiling.

The two averages have drifted together, which is unusual. The 50-day line tracks the short-term mood, while the 200-day line reflects the longer trend. Their convergence means recent gains have been erased, and the short-term picture has sunk to meet the long-term one. Bitcoin now sits roughly 17% under both, a wide gap that buyers would need to close before the trend could repair.

Over the past month, bitcoin has lost about 26%. Whatever demand returned over the summer has been overwhelmed by fresh selling since October.

Prices held roughly flat over the last 24 hours, a pause after the slide. A single quiet session after a sharp drop often reflects tired sellers rather than eager buyers. Nothing yet marks a turn higher, and the price sits closer to its floor than its ceiling.

Sellers Still Steer Despite Extreme Oversold Readings

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, stands near 19 on the daily chart. Readings below 30 count as oversold, so this one sits deep in that zone. Selling has run far and fast, and stretched markets often snap back briefly.

An oversold reading only flags exhaustion, though. It does not mark a bottom by itself. Prices can stay oversold for days when a trend is strong.

Momentum still points down, with the MACD gauge holding below its signal line. Trend-strength readings also confirm a real downtrend, and sellers are the ones driving it. Together, those signals say the pressure has not eased yet.

The weekly move shows the same picture. Bitcoin dropped about 13% over seven days, a pace that points to steady selling. Any bounce from these levels would first need to show up as a shift in momentum before it could be trusted.

Why $59K Matters More Than Any Fund Flow

Support sits near $59,000, a few thousand dollars under the current price. It is the only nearby floor, and no further support is mapped beneath it. A clean break would leave buyers without an obvious place to step in.

This is where the summer fund buying gets its real test. Institutions that added exposure in the third quarter now face losses on part of those positions. If that demand is still active, it should appear at this level. A failure to defend the level would suggest the earlier inflows have faded.

The upside map is clearer. The first ceiling matches the shared moving averages. Reclaiming that zone would put bitcoin back above both lines and turn them into support. Beyond it, resistance waits near $80,000. Both targets look distant for now.

Bounce or Breakdown in the Next 72 Hours

Two paths stand out for the coming days, and the support line decides which one plays out.

  • Bullish: Buyers defend the nearby floor and the oversold reading sparks a relief rally. That bounce could carry bitcoin back toward the shared moving averages overhead. A daily close under support would cancel this view.
  • Bearish: A daily close below support removes the only mapped floor and leaves open air beneath. Sellers would then keep control of the trend. A recovery above the two averages would invalidate this case.

Old Inflows Cannot Yet Outweigh Fresh Selling

The return of institutional buyers is a welcome sign from an earlier market. Sellers still control the trend, and that holds until bitcoin climbs back above its two moving averages.

Downside risk remains larger. If current support gives way, losses could gather speed quickly.

title: LINK Retests $8.8 as Bears Get Another Opening Despite UBS's Tokenized Note Pilot
description: UBS ran a live Chainlink pilot for a tokenized structured note, yet LINK keeps sliding. See why support near $7.83 is the level buyers must hold now.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • UBS ran a live pilot using Chainlink to automate a tokenized structured note on Ethereum.
  • LINK keeps sliding under both key moving averages, and momentum still favors sellers.
  • The nearest support near $7.83 is the floor buyers need to hold.

UBS has tested Chainlink in production. The bank plugged its existing systems into a blockchain without replacing them.

The pilot strengthens Chainlink's pitch to big banks, yet LINK has kept falling through the announcement. Traders now want to know whether a real adoption win can slow a month-long selloff. So far, sellers still hold the edge.

UBS Puts Chainlink to Work on a Live Structured Note

UBS has run a production pilot that uses Chainlink to automate the issuance and lifecycle management of a tokenized structured note on Ethereum. Chainlink announced the pilot on Nov 19, 2026.

The bank did not replace its existing systems. It connected its current banking infrastructure to the blockchain through the Chainlink Runtime Environment, known as CRE. That link gave UBS a real-time view of token balances, coupon entitlements, barrier proximity and product status.

This work extends UBS Tokenize, the bank's service for issuing tokenized assets on public chains. UBS plans to settle future notes through its own digital money products, but it has not set a launch date.

Chainlink estimates the global structured-products market at more than $2 trillion in outstanding notional. Johann Eid, chief business officer at Chainlink Labs, said banks can connect existing systems to blockchains through Chainlink. He said they can then automate issuing, servicing and settling these notes, which cuts operating costs.

Good News Lands on a Chart Still Sliding Under Both Averages

Chainlink (LINK) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

LINK traded near $8.89 at last check, down about 1% on the day. The token has given up roughly 28% over the past month. So far, traders have treated the UBS headline as background noise.

LINK fell about 12% over seven days, so selling kept going straight into the announcement. Buyers who might have used the news to step in mostly stayed on the sidelines.

Moving averages, which smooth out daily swings to show the broader trend, tell a similar story. The 50-day average sits near $10.92. The 200-day average is close by at about $10.84. Both lines now hang well above the price. When a coin trades under its key averages, those levels tend to act as a ceiling on rallies.

The two averages have nearly converged, which stacks resistance in one tight zone overhead. Any rebound would have to climb roughly 20% just to test that band. Until LINK gets back above it, sellers keep the upper hand.

Sellers Keep Momentum Even as RSI Nears Oversold

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits at 31. That reading is just above the 30 mark that signals oversold conditions. In plain terms, the selling has run hard and fast, and the token looks stretched to the downside.

Coins can hover near oversold for days while prices keep drifting lower. A low RSI shows sellers may be tiring, but it gives no sign that buyers have taken over.

Other gauges back that view. The MACD, a tool that tracks shifts in momentum, remains below its signal line, so momentum still points down. Trend strength readings also show a real trend, and sellers are the ones leading it.

A MACD cross back above its signal line would give the earliest hint that pressure is easing.

$7.83 Is the Floor Bulls Cannot Afford to Lose

The nearest support sits near $7.83, the line buyers need to defend. No mapped support lies beneath it, so a clean break would leave little in the way of further losses.

The next reference point is the 52-week low near $7.02. The yearly range has stretched as high as $15.74, which shows how much ground the token has surrendered.

Overhead, the first resistance stands near $10.27. Above it, the next barrier sits around $10.91, right on top of the 50-day line. Sellers would likely defend that stacked zone hard.

A daily close above that first barrier would signal a possible turn. Until then, rallies look like chances for sellers to reload.

What Flips the Script Over the Next Three Days

  • Bullish: A push through first resistance would open a run at the second barrier, right where the 50-day line sits. That would mark the first real break in the sellers' grip. The setup fails if LINK closes back below $8.8, which would return control to the bears.
  • Bearish: A daily close under the support floor would expose the yearly low and likely bring fresh selling. This view fails if LINK recovers above first resistance, which would signal buyers have returned.

Adoption Wins Headlines While Price Waits

The UBS pilot worked in production, which helps Chainlink's long-term case with banks. The chart still says sellers run the short-term trend until LINK reclaims resistance.

Risks remain. UBS has set no date for settling notes in its digital money, and wider crypto weakness could drag LINK lower whatever the headlines say.

title: HYPE Open Interest Hit $16.8B in Q3, Topping Bybit, as 1inch Joins In
description: 1inch added Hyperliquid perps to its wallet as open interest hit $16.8 billion. HYPE still trades below both averages, with support near $60 the level to watch.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • 1inch now offers Hyperliquid perpetual futures in its dApp and Android wallet, with iOS expected soon.
  • HYPE trades below both its 50-day and 200-day averages, and sellers still lead the trend.
  • The nearest support is the floor that matters most, with no mapped level beneath it.

Hyperliquid gained another major front end this week as 1inch plugged the venue's perpetual futures into its wallet and trading app. The rollout adds to a growing list of DeFi platforms routing traders to Hyperliquid.

For HYPE holders, the timing is awkward. Usage keeps climbing while the token keeps sliding, and momentum still favors sellers.

1inch Brings Hyperliquid Perps to Its Wallet and dApp

1inch has added Hyperliquid-powered perpetual futures to its dApp and Android wallet. The company said an iOS version should follow within weeks. Traders can access markets in crypto, stocks, commodities and forex. One contract tracks the expected price of Anthropic Class A shares before any IPO.

Funding works with tokens users already hold. 1inch converts them to USDC and deposits the result into the trader's Hyperliquid balance. Supported orders include market, limit, TWAP and stop-loss/take-profit. The wallet uses isolated margin by default, while the dApp runs on cross margin.

Demand behind the venue keeps growing. Data from the Hyperliquid Research Collective shows open interest rose nearly 80% from the end of June. It reached $16.8 billion in the third quarter. That total put Hyperliquid ahead of Bybit, Kraken and OKX.

Its share of open interest across itself and eight major exchanges climbed to 11.7% from 9.6%. Uniswap, Morpho and Curve already integrate these perps. NYSE parent ICE also plans Hyperliquid-based futures in the US.

Traders did not reward the news on the day. HYPE fell 3.62% and 1INCH dropped 4.66%.

Record Usage Meets a Price Stuck Under Both Averages

Hyperliquid (HYPE) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

HYPE traded near $65.82 at last check, down about 1% over the past 24 hours. The token sits below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. Those averages track the typical closing price over each period, so a coin under both is in a downtrend on short and long views alike.

The gap to the 50-day line is wide. That average stands near $77, roughly 15% above the current price. Recent buyers are mostly holding losses, and rallies toward that level may meet sellers looking to exit.

Losses have built steadily. HYPE lost about 9% over seven days and about 18% over 30 days.

Integrations with front ends such as 1inch bring new traders to the venue, and open interest keeps setting records. Yet the token has drifted lower through the same stretch.

Bulls first need to win back the 200-day average near $69.50. It sits only a few dollars above the price. A close above it would suggest the long-term trend is stabilizing. Until then, that line acts as a ceiling, and each failed test would hand sellers more confidence.

Sellers Still Set the Pace

Momentum readings back up what the averages show. The daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits at 34. That reading is weak, yet it remains above the 30 mark that usually signals oversold conditions. In plain terms, sellers have room to push further before the token looks stretched to the downside.

MACD, which compares a fast and a slow trend line, is still below its signal line. That means downside momentum has not faded. A cross back above would be the first hint of a turn, and it has not appeared.

Trend strength tells a similar story. The decline qualifies as a real trend, and sellers are the ones driving it. Bounces inside a seller-led trend tend to fade quickly.

Why $60.03 Matters More Than Any Headline

Support sits near $60, and the data shows no mapped floor below it. That makes it the level traders will watch most closely this week. A clean close under it would remove the last nearby cushion. Sellers who have pressed the trend so far could then speed up, with stop orders adding fuel.

One more weak session could put that support to the test. Holders who bought near the recent lows may defend it, but a seller-led trend often grinds through such zones.

Resistance near $74.50 is the upside marker. Reclaiming it would clear the 200-day line on the way and show buyers regaining control. From there, the next target sits near $82.60, which is above the 50-day average.

Two Paths for the Next Three Days

The next three days hinge on whether HYPE can win back the 200-day line or loses its nearest floor.

  • Bullish: A close above the 200-day average would show buyers regaining footing and put resistance in play. A slip back under the support floor discussed above would invalidate this case.
  • Bearish: A close below support would leave no mapped cushion and likely extend the slide. A recovery above resistance would invalidate this case and suggest sellers are losing control.

Adoption Is Winning While the Chart Lags

Hyperliquid keeps adding distribution, and 1inch's wallet rollout gives the venue another steady stream of traders. The token's chart still points the other way. Sellers hold the trend until HYPE clears the resistance level mapped above.

With no second floor in the data, a break of support could turn a slow grind into a fast drop.

title: Why Is ETH Down? Bitmine Reports a $6.3B Loss as Fed Hikes Weigh on Ethereum
description: Ether trades near $1,740 after Bitmine reported a $6.3 billion loss and neared its 5% buying cap. See the 50-day line and support levels traders are watching.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Bitmine, the largest corporate holder of Ether, reported a steep annual loss and has nearly maxed out its buying target.
  • Ether sits below both of its long moving averages, and momentum still favors sellers despite deeply oversold readings.
  • Traders are watching whether ETH can reclaim its 50-day line, the first ceiling standing between a bounce and real repair.

Bitmine Immersion Technologies, the Tom Lee-chaired firm that built a huge Ether treasury, reported a steep annual loss tied mostly to its ETH bets. The company now holds almost all the Ether its own target allows.

That leaves Ethereum without one of its most reliable dip buyers just as Fed tightening and stalled crypto legislation weigh on risk assets. So far, sellers keep control of the trend.

Ethereum's Biggest Corporate Buyer Runs Out of Room

Bitmine Immersion Technologies (NYSE: BMNR), chaired by Tom Lee, posted a $6.3 billion net loss for fiscal 2026. Most of that loss came from its Ether purchases. The fiscal year ended Aug. 31.

The company holds about 6,077,745 ETH, worth roughly $10.8 billion. That equals 4.97% of Ether's 122.2 million supply. Bitmine set a 5% target, so it has almost no room left to buy more and lower its average cost.

Bitmine started buying on June 30, 2025. Ether has dropped nearly 30% since then. BMNR shares have lost nearly half their value over 12 months. Lee first called ETH a buy in late 2024 at about $3,400.

The backdrop has turned harsher. The Federal Reserve raised rates in September, its first hike in three years, as the Iran war pushed up inflation. The CLARITY Act died in the Senate. A Democratic midterm sweep could also bring tighter rules for altcoins.

Lee still points to stablecoins, tokenized real-world assets and AI agents running on Ethereum. Those drivers may take longer to pay off. On Nov 19, ETH fell 3.69% and BMNR slid 4.65%.

ETH Trades Far Below Both Long Averages

Ethereum (ETH) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Ether traded near $1,740 at last check, down about 1% over the past day. The daily move looks small, but the market has been sliding for weeks.

The price sits far below its 50-day moving average, which stands around $2,190. A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the underlying trend. ETH also trades well under its 200-day average near $2,260. Both lines now act as ceilings.

Losses have picked up speed. Ether lost about 14% over seven days and roughly 29% over the past month. Most of that damage landed as the Bitmine results hit and rate worries spread across risk assets.

Trend strength readings back up that picture. The indicator that measures how firm a trend is shows a real, established move, and sellers lead it. Buyers have yet to mount a serious defense.

Momentum still points down as well. That leaves the 50-day line as the first level ETH would need to reclaim before traders could talk about a shift. For now, rallies toward those averages look more likely to meet selling than to break through.

Oversold Readings Have Not Stopped the Selling

Ether's daily RSI stands near 22. RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, flags a market as oversold below 30. That puts ETH deep in the zone where selling has run ahead of itself, and short relief bounces often start from there.

A bounce still needs buyers to show up. The MACD, which compares a fast and a slow trend line, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, downside momentum has not yet turned, even after weeks of losses.

Oversold markets can stay oversold for a long time when a trend is this firm. Traders watching for a turn will want MACD to cross back above its signal line first. Until then, any lift from these depressed readings may prove brief.

A Wide Gap Separates Buyers From the Next Floor

On the daily chart, the nearest support sits around $1,200. That level lies hundreds of dollars below the current price. Little stands in the way if sellers keep pressing.

The data shows no clear level beneath it. A break there would leave Ether without an obvious place for buyers to regroup.

Overhead, the first resistance sits near $2,170. That level lines up closely with the 50-day line, which makes it a double ceiling. Reclaiming it would mark the first real sign of repair after the recent slide.

The next hurdle sits around $2,280. A push through it would lift ETH back above the 200-day zone. Buyers would then have a stronger case that the downtrend had run its course.

Where the Next Three Days Could Take Ether

Two paths stand out for the coming sessions, and sellers hold the edge in both.

  • Bullish: An oversold bounce that clears the first resistance near the 50-day line would open a run toward the next hurdle by the 200-day zone. A slide back below today's trading range would cancel that setup.
  • Bearish: If Ether fails to recover, the lone support floor far below stays in play. A daily close above that first resistance would invalidate the bearish case.

Sellers Keep the Upper Hand for Now

The trend stays bearish until Ether wins back its 50-day and 200-day lines. Deeply oversold readings may spark a bounce, but they do not change the direction on their own.

Timing remains the main risk. Bitmine has almost no buying room left, and higher rates keep pressure on risk assets. Sharp relief rallies could fade fast without a large buyer behind them.

title: Son of prominent California chef loses leg after suspected drunken driver plows into pedestrians
description: Ziggy Molteni, son of chef Mariano Molteni, lost his leg in an alleged Laguna Beach drunk driving crash and faces more surgeries, his family says.
fullContent:
The son of a prominent chef in California lost his leg after he was hit by an alleged drunken driver, according to his family.

Two men were hit by a car on Saturday morning following a crash in Laguna Beach, California, police told the Orange County Register. A family friend of the victim posted in a GoFundMe that the victim, Ziggy Molteni, was pinned beneath the car and lost his right lower leg.

The suspected driver of the car, who police say was drunk, was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence. The incident happened outside San Lorenzo Bikinis.

A separate GoFundMe from a family friend says that Frank Laptin is the second victim of the alleged DUI crash. Laptin has 18 broken bones, a crushed right foot, multiple left foot fractures, a broken leg and broken shoulder.

MULTIPLE DEAD AFTER VEHICLE CRASHES INTO FOOD STAND NEAR NORTH HOLLYWOOD METRO STATION

Ziggy Molteni is the son of Mariano Molteni, a well-known Orange County chef. He owns Tierra de Fuegos, an Argentine-style restaurant.

According to the fundraiser, Ziggy Molteni will have to undergo more surgeries and faces a "very long road to recovery."

"Since the accident just happened, there are still many unknowns regarding Ziggy's long-term care, recovery, and the costs that lie ahead," the fundraiser states. "A situation like this is something that none of us want to imagine being faced with."

The fundraiser has surpassed $180,000 in donations.

Ziggy Molteni recently graduated from Chapman University and is currently working to get his master's degree.

title: 1,800-year-old Roman toddler's grave found frozen in time, and it still had toys inside
description: A Roman child burial in the Tomis necropolis revealed clay toys, bronze amulets and flower garlands preserved for 1,800 years in an intact sarcophagus in Romania.
fullContent:
Archaeologists in Romania have unsealed an intact 1,800-year-old Roman child's sarcophagus — finding clay toys, protective amulets and preserved flower garlands buried alongside the toddler's remains.

The discovery was announced by the Museum of National History and Archaeology Constanța (MINAC) in late October, with additional details released in early November by Romania's Ministry of Culture.

The find was made during archaeological excavations in the city's Flămânda area, ahead of the construction of a private residential building.

7,000-YEAR-OLD BONES UNCOVERED AT CONSTRUCTION SITE IN STARTLING FIND

On-site archaeologists Constantin Băjenaru and Cătălin Nopcea first spotted signs of an intact sarcophagus on Oct. 22, before unearthing it and moving it to a museum facility, according to a translated statement from the museum. 

It wasn't until a few days later, on Oct. 27, that conservators, archaeologists and restoration specialists at MINAC opened the stone sarcophagus — revealing a nail-free wooden coffin inside.

Officials say the grave dates to between the second and third centuries A.D., and was located near an important ancient road on the northern edge of the ancient Tomis necropolis.

In its statement, Romania's Ministry of Culture said the child was estimated to be between 1 and 3 years old at the time of death.

ANCIENT ROMAN TREASURE UNEARTHED AT MILITARY BASE, TWO COINS AREN'T WHAT THEY SEEM

"The skeleton, measuring approximately 63 centimeters in length, appears to have been preserved in good condition, and numerous locks of hair were also discovered in the cranial area," ministry officials said in a translated release.

The body had been wrapped in textiles, a burial treatment officials compared to mummification.

"The way the tomb was sealed contributed to the preservation of materials that, under ordinary conditions, degrade over time," ministry officials said, noting the limestone lid was secured with lead clamps and waterproof mortar.

POMPEII HOME BURIED BY MOUNT VESUVIUS YIELDS PERSONAL TREASURES UNTOUCHED FOR NEARLY 2,000 YEARS

Inside the burial, archaeologists found clay toys, flower garlands, and bronze jewelry and amulets.

Photos from the excavation show the remains of the toys: a clay rooster and a small horse on wheels, both bearing traces of paint.

Other items inside the burial included a bone button, two bronze bracelets, a piece of gold foil engraved with magical symbols and a pair of bronze bullae — protective amulets Roman children wore to ward off evil spirits.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Archaeologists also recovered fragile organic remains from the tomb, including plant stems, folded bundles of plants and fabric strung onto a wooden support and a piece of cord that may have been used to pull the wheeled toy horse.

"These are details that transform an archaeological discovery into an encounter with the everyday life of people in antiquity," ministry officials said.

"Behind the funerary objects emerges the image of a childhood cut short too soon and of those who wished to preserve a part of it."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

While further testing could shed light on the burial rituals and materials used, officials said the child's identity — and the story behind their early death — remains lost to history.

"We do not know who the child's parents were, what the child's name was or what the cause of death was," the ministry said.

"However, we know — thanks to the objects discovered — that the burial was accompanied by gestures of love and a very carefully prepared ritual."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Looking ahead, MINAC officials are partnering with specialized restoration labs in Bucovina and Iași to preserve the fragile textiles and wooden coffin.

"Although we are still at the beginning of the documentation process, we consider this discovery to be an important one, first and foremost due to the intact preservation of the sarcophagus," museum officials said.

"The untouched preservation of the funerary inventory ... offers valuable information regarding Roman-era funerary practices in Tomis."

title: America's largest IPO ever carries potentially seismic implications for political spending ahead of 2028
description: Anthropic makes its stock market debut Thursday at a $1.5 trillion valuation as its seven co-founders each pledge to give away 80% of their equity.
fullContent:
Anthropic’s Thursday stock market debut, valued at around $1.5 trillion, is the largest in American history and, given promises made by its founders, is likely the preface to a similarly historic flood of cash into the political system.

Bloomberg projects that each of Anthropic’s seven co-founders will be worth approximately $24.5 billion now that their artificial intelligence firm has gone public. Each of the seven has also pledged to give away 80% of their equity in the firm to philanthropic causes — a promise that has raised eyebrows given Anthropic’s links to a controversial moral philosophy and its history of spending big to influence elections.

Effective altruism, which some of Anthropic’s early funders and employees have voiced support for, generally treats massive political and philanthropic giving as a moral obligation to prevent AI "doomsday" scenarios, such as a rogue agent working to exterminate the human race. Though the company's founders have distanced themselves from the movement, some early employees and other figures associated with Anthropic have maintained connections to its ideas, particularly its emphasis on preventing potentially catastrophic risks from artificial intelligence.

Politically, this has manifested as Anthropic's leaders throwing large sums of money behind efforts to regulate AI development. This approach has often put Anthropic at odds with the White House and its Republican allies, who are pursuing unchained innovation to spur economic growth, a dynamic that could become even more tense now that the firm’s leaders have billions of dollars at their disposal.

ANTHROPIC CEO CALLS ON AI INDUSTRY TO SLOW DOWN TECH RACE, DRAWING SUPPORT FROM ELON MUSK, SAM ALTMAN

A Fox News Digital analysis of campaign finance filings found that Anthropic employees donated about $7.1 million to Democrats and Democratic-aligned committees, compared to just around $3.7 million to Republicans and Republican-aligned committees during the 2026 electoral cycle.

Such a split is noteworthy given that Anthropic offers to match shares donated by its employees by contributing additional shares to the organizations they opt to support. If the firm’s employees decide to give large chunks of equity to left-of-center organizations, for instance, it would result in a significant Anthropic-funded financial windfall for the left.

"I think there’s a lot of overlap between certain left-of-center causes," Nathan Leamer, a consultant who works on tech policy, told Fox News Digital when asked about the political orientation of Anthropic’s employees and effective altruists more broadly. "They've benefited from capitalism, but their worldviews do not always reflect free market values."

TECH POWERHOUSE’S REGULATORY PUSH BEARS SIMILARITIES TO A NOTORIOUS WASHINGTON STRATEGY

While Anthropic's rank-and-file employees appear to favor Democrats in their political donations, some of the company's most prominent financial contributions have gone toward a political network seeking to influence both parties around AI regulation, rather than exclusively supporting one partisan side.

Anthropic’s founders and longtime employees have comparatively little in the way of direct partisan donations, with much of their money being directed toward Public First, a super PAC network that supports candidates in both parties who favor stronger AI safeguards.

Defending Our Values PAC, on the right, and the Jobs and Democracy PAC, on the left, spent millions of dollars influencing Republican and Democratic primary elections during the 2026 cycle to boost candidates seeking to advance safety-related AI regulations. The Democratic PAC spent far more, around $20 million, than its GOP-focused counterpart, which paid out just under $8 million.

As 2028 approaches, the seven co-founders' newly acquired fortunes could give them substantially greater financial capacity to support causes and organizations they believe in — and presidential primaries will be a natural target for their newly acquired war chests.

In the general election, whichever candidate takes a position more aligned with Anthropic’s preferred regulatory stance may be able to count on large sums to back their bid for the White House. The new funds also enable Anthropic and its allies to focus on a much broader range of down-ballot races to win more allies in Congress and state legislatures.

HOUSE COMMITTEE PASSES FOREIGN FUNDING TRANSPARENCY ACT TO EXPOSE FOREIGN DONATIONS TO NONPROFITS

Explicitly political organizations aren’t the only ones likely to see their coffers swell from the deluge of cash.

A cottage industry of think tanks and advocacy organizations has sprung up in D.C. and San Francisco to conduct research and make arguments aimed at convincing those with power of the merits of robust AI safety regulation. Many nonprofit advocacy organizations, including 501(c)(4) groups such as Public First Action, are not required to publicly disclose their donors, making it difficult to identify the full network of individuals and organizations financing the push for AI regulation. Anthropic, however, made its initial $40 million donation to Public First Action to support such education and policy work.

"I can tell you among civil society — think tanks and foundations and other organizations in the nonprofit world — this is absolutely making an impact," Leamer told Fox News Digital when asked about this dynamic. "I was in a conversation last night with a conservative organization who was telling me they're being offered hundreds of thousands of dollars to engage in a more [effective altruist]-aligned worldview, even though it's not necessarily where they are philosophically … If that’s happening among people I’m talking to, I can’t imagine how many more they’re talking to."

AI 'DOOMERS' RISK KNEECAPPING US VS CHINA, BUT EX-PENTAGON VET SAYS BOTH EXTREMES MISS THE MARK

An individual close to the think tank world, requesting to remain anonymous, told Fox News Digital that donors aligned with Anthropic and effective altruism are already attempting to throw money around with the aim of influencing conservative thought leaders. In their telling, prospective funders will approach right-of-center organizations and offer them funding to research topics they are already interested in, such as child safety, then use that grant funding as leverage to influence their messaging.

Much of this messaging has been oriented toward pushing regulation to slow AI development so that engineers can devise mechanisms to stop the technology from being used for evil, or from inadvertently hurting people.

Anthropic’s leaders maintain that such regulations are necessary to prevent AI from harming humanity, whereas its detractors argue that such guardrails will kneecap America’s ability to compete with China. Some critics have argued that Anthropic is pushing for safety laws as a way to create rules that it can then exploit to give itself a leg up over rivals.

WHO IS DARIO AMODEI, THE ANTHROPIC CEO PUSHING INDEPENDENT AI OVERSIGHT?

Some have traced Anthropic’s caution toward AI development to the effective altruist movement, which itself has segments who predict that unregulated advancement in the field may bring about the end of humanity.

Critics of effective altruism, which holds that individuals should seek out the avenue through which they can do the most good for each dollar spent, argue that its emphasis on speculative threats, including catastrophic artificial intelligence, can divert resources from immediate problems such as poverty.

In its extreme manifestation, some effective altruists have argued that one of the most efficient ways to engage in charitable giving is by improving the welfare of shrimp, as hundreds of billions of shrimp are farmed annually, so even modest improvements in how they are treated could reduce enormous amounts of suffering at relatively little cost. Mainstream effective altruists, however, generally argue that funds should be directed toward researching AI safety given the near-infinite negative downside of the technology destroying humanity.

That Anthropic’s leaders will actually open their pocketbooks to the extent promised, or even to these causes in particular, is not guaranteed. The IPO’s prospectus calls the commitments "voluntary, revocable expressions" of philanthropic intent that "do not constitute legally binding obligations."

Their ability to spend will also be dependent on Anthropic’s stock holding value amid a turbulent political and economic environment.

Anthropic and Public First Action did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Thursday.

title: Ethereum Lost $1,000 in 7 Weeks: What’s Going On?
description:
Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) has dropped from near $2,750 to $1,750 in just seven weeks, a 36% slide that has erased its entire August rally.
Binance Inflows Signal Short-Term Selling Pressure
Ethereum’s long-term staking numbers still look healthy, with ETH 2.0 staking transactions continuing to climb, according to CryptoQuant contributor PelinayPA, a trend that suggests investors would rather lock up their ETH than sell it.
The shorter-term picture tells a different story, since Binance recorded 17,485 ETH in net inflows while the price fell, which PelinayPA said increases the likelihood that some holders are moving ETH onto the exchange to trade or sell.
Exchange inflows do not always lead to immediate selling, but they often rise when traders prepare to exit or reposition. This wave remains below the levels seen during previous periods of heavy selling, suggesting real but still moderate pressure.
Fundamentals Have Grown, But The Price Hasn’t Followed
Crypto trader Ash Crypto pointed out a widening gap between Ethereum’s on-chain growth and its price, comparing the ecosystem then and now:
2021: ETH near $1,400, $0 in total value locked, about $30 million in stablecoins, no major institutional adoption, no sizable DeFi ecosystem, no ETFs
2026: ETH near $1,800, roughly $40 billion in TVL, $131 billion in stablecoins, growing institutional interest, thousands of active dApps, multiple spot ETFs
Despite that buildout, Ether’s price is up only about 30% since then.
Key Levels To Watch on Ethereum’s Chart
Ethereum is approaching the rising trendline from June’s lows, now sitting near $1,710 to $1,720, the level traders are watching most closely. 
A daily close below it would open the door to $1,600, then $1,500.
Buyers need to reclaim $1,800 to $1,850 to give any rebound real room to run, with stronger resistance sitting near $2,000, where the 20-day EMA and Parabolic SAR converge.

title: CFP selection committee 'explains' its lack of transparency: isn't really 'feasible' | Ian Miller
description: The College Football Playoff selection committee kept Alabama football steady while Indiana football dropped five spots on a bye, sparking bias claims.
fullContent:
The move from the BCS to a College Football Playoff selection committee was supposed to limit controversy and disagreement about the teams chosen to play for a championship.

Instead? It's been the exact opposite. As the selection committee's rankings thus far in the 2026-2027 season have demonstrated, the controversy has only deepened. There's been clear favoritism, bias, subjectivity and inconsistency. Best exemplified by the disastrous release of week three of the committee's top-25 poll, which revealed that they have no intention of maintaining their standards when they apply to teams in the SEC. Nor will they listen to criticism and adjust their thinking.

The Indiana Hoosiers in week two of the poll dropped five spots on a bye week, because the Big Ten opponents they'd beaten this season all lost in the same week. The exact same thing happened to the Alabama Crimson Tide, but worse, and the committee not only didn't drop them, committee chair Hunter Yurachek praised them.

CFP HANGOVER: INDIANA CAN’T ESCAPE SCHEDULE DEBATE, BUT ALABAMA GETS TO SKIP THE CONVERSATION ONCE AGAIN

Why? Because of their resilient road performance against ... Vanderbilt. In a stadium that was roughly 60% Alabama fans, the Tide had one of the worst games of the season. The Commodores actually drove into the Alabama red zone more frequently throughout the game, three to two. The vaunted Alabama offense had just 309 total yards with an anemic 4.5 yards per play. Their rushing "attack" was even worse, averaging just 2.6 yards per attempt.

This came against a team that is now 1-6 in the SEC and should be 3-7 overall, if not for one of the most bizarre, fluky finishes in recent college football memory against NC State. Vanderbilt is bad! The game was effectively a home one, thanks to the enormous road game crowd advantage. And the Tide still played poorly, while all their other Patented SEC Quality Wins™ lost. Sounds like a recipe for a team to fall in the rankings, right?

CFP SELECTION COMMITTEE HAS OFFICIALLY DISCREDITED ITSELF WITH LATEST RANKINGS | IAN MILLER

Wrong. The Tide are under the committee's protection, and the comments from Yurachek afterward explained it beautifully.

"Alabama faced a similar circumstance where five of their SEC opponents all lost, but it didn't have the same impact on their strength of schedule that it had on Indiana's strength of schedule," he said. "Actually, it is very minimal for Alabama because of the quality and the strength of schedule of those five teams that lost."

South Carolina firmly established that it is not good by losing to an atrocious Arkansas team by 28 points. Texas A&M is still treated as a Quality Win™ because it plays in the SEC, despite falling to 4-6 and 1-6 in conference. Mississippi State has lost five games in a row, allowing an average of 35 points per game. It is still counted as a Quality Win™ because of a quarterback injury, since defense doesn't matter. Kentucky has lost two games in a row and scored just 20 combined points, demonstrating that, as the computer metrics always suggested, it was wildly overrated to begin with. Oh, and LSU lost yet again at home, falling to 3-4 in the SEC and 6-4 overall.

No serious person would argue that Alabama's resume or strength of schedule or record looks better this week than it did last week. But there are no serious people on the College Football Playoff selection committee.

What makes this nonsense even more frustrating is the lack of transparency around the process. Yurachek frequently mentions things like "pods" and "metrics" and "strength of schedule" in his absurdist interviews, yet never explains what those pods are, how they're created, what metrics they use, how they calculate strength of schedule, or what goes into their thought process other than "SEC GOOD ME LIKE SEC RANKED WINS."

This week, he credited Bama for avoiding an emotional letdown after beating LSU. What? Are we measuring emotions now? How does this work? Do they have, like, a Whoop that they use to track the heart rate of players and coaches in the SEC, and if it's elevated, they get special pod points? Or is there a color wheel that the committee uses to track emotions and make decisions on? Do they measure emotions in other conferences or just the SEC? Shouldn't Utah move up to No. 1 because they followed up an emotional win over BYU with a road win over a ranked team?

He also said something about Alabama's margin of victory in SEC games, which is so beyond dumb it beggars belief. The margins of victory can be extremely misleading, which is why advanced metric systems look at more important factors like game efficiency, scoring outside of garbage time, and success rate on offense, success rate allowed on defense, and special teams advantages.

Sarcasm and Yurachek's nonsensical statements aside, though, this has raised a more salient and important question: what metrics do they actually use? How do they determine strength of schedule?

ESPN's Heather Dinich gave an explanation so ridiculous that even her colleagues at the network made fun of her for it. But what's actually happening here?

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Per a source, the committee uses 30 "metrics" to come up with their strength of schedule and strength of record ratings. It'd be great if fans could see what those metrics are, as that would allow more qualified, experienced, and competent fans and analysts to look at them and evaluate them.

Thankfully, reporter Chris Vannini asked them about this week. And their answer was, well, as usual, awful.

Yurachek responded first, saying that it's "something that we've talked about," then added, "But right now that's kind of been the guidelines that those aren't shared publicly."

Why not? Why are they not shared publicly? Is it because they know that they'd be humiliated ... again ... and the public would see how slanted they are towards the SEC? Things like "ranked wins" and "ranked conference wins," which lead to circular reasoning with SEC teams starting the preseason overrated and providing those benefits to their opponents?

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Rich Clark, the committee's executive director, chimed in, saying, "Just to let you know, we have not provided those publicly. Basically, there's so many metrics, to really give that out publicly with an explanation of them isn't really feasible now.

"It is something that we're considering. We're looking at this in the off-season to see what metrics and how we would present those potentially in the coming seasons."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Why is it not feasible? Do they not have internet connections? Is it too tough for them to create a PDF? We have AI now, run it through ChatGPT or Gemini or Claude or Grok and give us a one-page summary and description. This isn't hard! It's extremely easy! And feasible!

The problem is, of course, that the committee does not want people to see how bad their "metrics" are. How ridiculous it is to make decisions with tens of millions of dollars on the line based on things that informed fans and analysts knew weren't important decades ago. How their inconsistent "logic" and incoherent "reasoning" creates hypocrisy, double standards, no standards, bias, and ultimately, controversy.

Yes, it's all well and good that we have athletic directors and former players and coaches on the committee. What do we actually need? Well, should this system continue, which it shouldn't, are people with an analytical background. Who create metrics and understand efficiency and success rate.

Not, "Those Bama boys sure were emotionally drained after that game, see look at their mood rings, we have to reward them for playing like garbage." That's nonsense. Not, "Alabama's margin of victory is the second best in the SEC, so we need to rank them No. 3 despite other more deserving teams being behind them." Because that's insane and meaningless. Not, "we invented Missouri and South Carolina and Florida and Oklahoma as good teams, then based our rankings off that false assumption." Because that's insulting.

Transparency should be the bare minimum, and they can't even do that. They'll "consider" doling out some information to the peasants, next year, if we behave and don't criticize them too much. They learn nothing, they change nothing, they say nothing of value. It's a joke, and it's why the whole thing needs to be torn down.

The campaign is built around the first trade, which is often the main hurdle for new users. New users can receive up to 400 USDT in combined welcome rewards across spot and futures, while existing traders can compete for leaderboard prizes.

Loss Protection for New Spot and Futures Traders

For spot trading, newly registered users with no prior spot trades who make a first purchase of at least 50 USDT in BTC or ETH, and hold it until the campaign ends, are covered if the price is at least 20% below their purchase price at the end of the campaign. Bitrue covers the actual loss up to 100 USDT, paid as a futures trial bonus, once per user.

For futures trading, new users receive two benefits:

  • Position trial voucher: a 100 USDT position trial voucher after a first futures trade of at least 100 USDT, available on a first-come, first-served basis.
  • Liquidation protection: if a position is liquidated during the campaign, Bitrue compensates the lost margin on the largest single loss, up to 200 USDT. Protection applies once per trader, to BTC, ETH, XRP and SOL positions with leverage of 10x or lower.

Two Leaderboards With 40,000 USDT in Prizes

The campaign also includes two leaderboards ranked by trading volume:

  • Futures leaderboard: the top 100 traders by futures volume share a 30,000 USDT prize pool, with larger shares for higher ranks. Traders need at least 500 USDT in futures volume to qualify. Prizes include enhanced futures trial bonuses and position trial vouchers.

Traders who reach a combined 2,000 USDT in spot and futures volume during the campaign can unlock a Black Friday Surprise Box, drawn from a 10,000 USDT reward pool. Physical prizes are limited and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, and are paid out in the equivalent value in USDT.

Eligibility and Distribution

Participants register through the campaign page. After the campaign ends, Bitrue will confirm eligible users within 10 business days, and rewards and trial bonuses will be credited to their spot and futures accounts. Accounts involved in bulk sign-ups from the same device or IP address, or in wash trading, are not eligible. Final rewards are subject to Bitrue’s review.

Futures trading involves significant risk, and loss protection under the campaign is limited to the conditions and caps set out in the campaign rules.

title: Lumentum CEO Says Marvell Deal Is ‘Even More Powerful’ Despite Stock Selloff
description:
Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE) and Marvell Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) are trying to reassure investors about their planned $115 billion all-stock combination after both stocks suffered steep declines amid deal concerns and a broader selloff across AI semiconductor names.
Hurlston Defends The Combination
Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston defended the transaction, arguing that both companies continue to perform well and that the combined business would be stronger.
"Their numbers are phenomenal. Our numbers are phenomenal, and we feel the combination is even more powerful," Hurlston told CNBC’s Jim Cramer.
He also acknowledged the negative shareholder reaction. "Shareholders are not happy … It’s been a tough couple of weeks," Hurlston said.
Marvell and Lumentum shares have fallen 45% and 42%, respectively, since the Oct. 28 close, when Bloomberg reported that Marvell was nearing an acquisition of Lumentum.
The stocks have also lost roughly 30%-40% over the past month amid broader weakness across AI-related semiconductor stocks.
The companies formally announced the transaction on Nov. 2. The all-stock deal implied an enterprise value of $115 billion for Lumentum and is expected to close in the first half of 2028.
Fiber Shift Underpins Deal Strategy
Hurlston said the combination brings together Marvell’s semiconductor and networking technology with Lumentum’s optical components as AI data centers increasingly move from copper connections toward fiber optics.
He said that transition, rather than simply an increase in the number of data centers, could become an important growth driver for the combined company.
Earnings And S-4 Could Reassure Investors
Hurlston acknowledged that management must do more to convince shareholders. "We’ve got work to do with our shareholders," he said.
He pointed to Marvell’s Dec. 1 earnings report, Lumentum’s upcoming results and the merger-related S-4 filing as opportunities to show investors how both businesses are performing.
Hurlston said those disclosures could show that "there’s nothing wrong here," adding that the companies are "even better together."
Marvell is expected to report EPS of $1.09, up from 76 cents a year earlier, on revenue of $3.16 billion, compared with $2.08 billion in the prior-year period.
Lumentum Results Show Demand Remains Strong
Hurlston said Lumentum has not seen a slowdown in demand despite broader questions around AI infrastructure spending.
On Nov. 2, Lumentum reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 adjusted earnings of $4.57 per share, above the $4.19 estimate, while revenue of $1.263 billion topped expectations of $1.249 billion.
Hurlston said stronger financial performance from both companies could eventually help restore their valuation multiples.
Regulatory Risk Remains
Separately, Bloomberg analysts previously expressed skepticism about whether the transaction would close, citing uncertainty around China’s regulatory review.
Price Action: Lumentum Holdings shares were down 6.06% at $502.70, and Marvell Technology shares were down 5.04% at $131.48 during premarket trading on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: Bitcoin-Backed Lending Goes Live On Sui As Hashi Launches With 20+ Partners
description: Bitcoin holders have a new way to access liquidity without selling their BTC. Hashi, a Bitcoin finance infrastructure protocol built on Sui, has officially launched on mainnet with more than 20 partners supporting lending, custody, and decentralized financial services. The launch marks an important development for Bitcoin-backed lending, transforming a previously experimental system into infrastructure […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin holders have a new way to access liquidity without selling their BTC. Hashi, a Bitcoin finance infrastructure protocol built on Sui, has officially launched on mainnet with more than 20 partners supporting lending, custody, and decentralized financial services.

The launch marks an important development for Bitcoin-backed lending, transforming a previously experimental system into infrastructure supporting live financial applications.

Announced on November 19, the rollout includes institutional custody provider Anchorage Digital, lending protocol Fluid, and asset management platforms HoneyB and Upshift.

More importantly, Bitcoin holders can now use BTC-backed tokens as collateral to borrow stablecoins, potentially unlocking liquidity while maintaining their exposure to Bitcoin.

Bitcoin Lending Moves From Testnet To Mainnet

Hashi’s infrastructure connects Bitcoin with financial applications operating on Sui.

Users deposit Bitcoin through the protocol’s custody and signing arrangements, allowing an equivalent amount of hBTC to be issued on Sui. Each hBTC represents a claim backed by Bitcoin at a 1:1 ratio.

That representation can then be used in decentralized lending markets.

Fluid is among the first platforms offering live Bitcoin-backed borrowing, allowing eligible users to deposit hBTC as collateral and borrow USDC.

This means investors can potentially obtain dollar-denominated liquidity without immediately selling their Bitcoin holdings.

The development follows earlier reports about Hashi’s planned mainnet launch, when the project announced more than $500 million in capital commitments from participating institutions.

However, committed capital should not be confused with actual deposits or lending volume. The launch establishes infrastructure; sustained borrowing activity will determine its commercial significance.

Anchorage Digital And Institutional Partners Expand Bitcoin’s Utility

One of the more significant aspects of Hashi’s launch is the involvement of institutional infrastructure providers.

Anchorage Digital supports access through its Porto self-custody wallet, allowing institutions to interact with hBTC-based financial applications.

The company also plans additional settlement capabilities in early 2027.

Meanwhile, HoneyB has introduced Bitcoin and stablecoin vaults using Upshift’s infrastructure. These products aim to connect digital asset holders with managed financial strategies.

Other participating projects include Bluefin, Cetus, Current, and Suilend, which are developing additional Bitcoin-backed markets.

According to the official Sui Foundation announcement, the ecosystem includes more than 20 participants spanning custody, lending, trading, and asset management.

For Bitcoin, this represents another attempt to extend its usefulness beyond conventional trading and long-term storage.

Could Bitcoin-Backed Loans Reduce Selling Pressure?

The broader implications extend beyond one blockchain launch.

Bitcoin investors traditionally have two straightforward options when they need liquidity: sell part of their holdings or borrow against them through a financial intermediary.

Protocols such as Hashi introduce additional borrowing infrastructure, allowing BTC exposure to support loans and other financial products.

This trend is also emerging in alternative Bitcoin lending models, reflecting growing interest in making Bitcoin useful as productive collateral.

In theory, borrowing against Bitcoin could reduce the need for some holders to sell during periods when they require cash.

However, that outcome is not guaranteed.

Borrowers face interest costs, collateral requirements, liquidation risks, and potential losses from smart contract or cross-chain infrastructure failures.

A sharp Bitcoin price decline could trigger liquidations, creating selling pressure rather than reducing it.

A New Chapter For Bitcoin Finance?

Hashi’s mainnet launch demonstrates how Bitcoin is increasingly becoming collateral for financial services operating beyond its original blockchain.

With more than 20 partners involved, the project has established an ecosystem for borrowing, custody, and managed investment products.

The next important indicators will be the amount of BTC deposited, actual stablecoin borrowing, collateral utilization, and whether institutional participation develops into sustained activity.

For long-term Bitcoin supporters, the opportunity is significant: BTC could become more useful without requiring holders to abandon their underlying investment.

But the strongest evidence of success will come from measurable adoption, not launch announcements alone.
