title: Coinbase Targets In-House Prediction Markets as Shares Sink to 2023 Levels
description:
Coinbase Global Inc. (NASDAQ:COIN) is aiming to launch its own prediction markets in the U.S. by the first half of 2027, even as its stock slides back to levels last seen in late 2023.
Coinbase currently offers prediction markets through a partnership with Kalshi, but building its own version would let the company control what it lists and keep more of the trading revenue for itself, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. 
The plan would open the contracts to both retail and institutional customers.
Moreover, Coinbase agreed in December 2025 to buy The Clearing Company, a prediction markets startup, and already runs a regulated derivatives exchange after winning CFTC approval for its own clearinghouse in September. 
Chief Financial Officer Alesia Haas said in October that Coinbase planned to offer some of its own event contracts without giving a timeline, and a company spokesperson said there’s "nothing new to announce" on the launch date.
The financials back up the push, with event contracts topping a $200 million annualized revenue run rate in the third quarter, a business Haas called ‘one of our fastest-growing new revenue products’ on Coinbase’s October earnings call.
Coinbase Shares Sink To 2023 Levels
Coinbase stock has fallen nearly 15% this week and slipped another 1.5% in premarket trading Friday to $107, putting it roughly 76% below its 2025 peak near $445. 
The stock is now breaking below its $115-$125 support zone, and failing to reclaim that range keeps $100 in play, with the 2023 trading band near $80 to $90 as the next cushion below it.
Weekly RSI has dropped to 30.48, nearing oversold territory, though selling pressure hasn’t reversed yet. 
A recovery above $125 would help the chart, but the falling trendline and 20-week EMA near $160 stand in the way.
Benzinga reported Thursday that Milk Road analyst Martin, who sold his Coinbase shares months ago, said Robinhood (NASDAQ:HOOD) has won over most active traders, and he’s still waiting for a cheaper valuation before buying Coinbase back. 
Martin sees the company’s USDC (CRYPTO: USDC) push through its Circle partnership and its expanding custody business as ways to lean less on trading volume, though he expects fintech rivals Revolut and Nubank to make competing for U.S. customers even tougher.

The post Crypto Trader Goes 0 for 10: Every Single Trade Lost, and $192,500 Vanished appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
One crypto trader just pulled off a rare feat: ten trades, ten losses. According to on-chain tracker Lookonchain, the perfect losing streak wiped out about $192,500.

No position ended in profit, and not one even broke even. One trade alone did most of the damage.

Inside the Crypto Trader’s Perfect Losing Streak

Lookonchain shared the wallet address on X so that anyone can verify the sequence of failed trades. As a result, the record quickly drew attention across the crypto community.

The most brutal trade involved DCTY. The wallet spent about $214,700 accumulating the token. Roughly 20 minutes later, it sold the entire position.

That rapid exit locked in a loss of about $162,800, or nearly 76%. Moreover, that single trade accounted for most of the overall losses. It turned a series of smaller misses into a six-figure hit. The other nine tokens added roughly $29,700 in further losses.

“10 trades 10 losses hurts to even read. the trenches are no joke rn, sizing small is the only way i survive them,” one user said on X.

The speed of the drop shows how quickly capital can vanish in volatile or thinly traded tokens.

Why Do Some Traders Lose on Every Position?

Most traders post mixed results, with wins and losses spread over time. Going ten for ten on the downside is rare, even in crypto.

Such a run usually points to poor timing or aggressive entries into fading narratives. Bad luck, combined with large position sizes, can also play a role.

The same volatile period hurt other traders too. High-profile trader James Wynn got liquidated five times. Still, he holds about $3.14 million in long positions across Bitcoin and S&P 500-linked contracts.

His Bitcoin liquidation level sits near $60,177. While Wynn shows resilience under leverage, the anonymous wallet stands out for its consistent failure.

Ultimately, the episode highlights the risks of fast, high-conviction bets on speculative tokens. Without a clear edge or risk management, short-term trading can backfire.

On public blockchains, those losses also become visible almost instantly. As a result, such trades turn into public case studies for other investors.

title: Russian missiles hit Poland as Moscow unleashes a massive attack on Ukraine
description:
Ukrainian officials reported more than 80 missiles and 400 drones were fired (Handout)
Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least six people were killed in the capital, and neighbouring Poland reporting two Russian missiles likely landed in the south-east corner of the NATO country, accusing Moscow of a "provocation." 
Hours earlier, Russia's Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" response to Kyiv's strikes on Moscow's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China's Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. 
Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky called the night-time strikes one of Moscow's largest of the entire war, denouncing Russian "terror."
Zelensky -- who met with allies in Berlin Thursday -- said Putin's attempts to "redraw the world" with Xi and Trump had been a "failure."
In China, Putin said he "shared responsibility" for global peace with Xi and Trump and issued a "declaration toward peace" that made no mention of Moscow's almost five-year invasion of Ukraine.
AFP journalists saw people hunkering in Kyiv's metro stations -- which double as overnight air-raid shelters -- sleeping on yoga mats, camping chairs and in pop-up tents.
Kateryna Liubychenko, 32, had taken her toddler down to try to get some sleep through the bombardment.
"It's painful to have to stop our child from living," she told AFP.
Another two people were killed in Lviv, power was knocked out in swathes of the country and in Kyiv, three vital transport bridges were hit, officials said. 
Explosions rang out through the night as Ukrainian officials reported more than 80 missiles and 400 drones were fired.
"Kyiv: The death toll from last night's Russian attack has risen to six. Another 15 people were injured," Ukraine's emergency service said amid the rescue operation.
Three bridges that cross the Dnipro river were also hit, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, threatening yet more disruption to daily life in the city.
France requested a UN Security Council meeting over the strikes, saying "Russia will have to answer for its actions there." 
 
- Poland decries 'provocation' -
 
In neighbouring Poland, authorities said one missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec, with another missile and a jet-powered drone suspected to have hit two other locations.  
Warsaw said no-one was hurt. 
Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the weapons flying into Poland were deliberate.
"The provocation may have been linked with the fact that there are (military) exercises taking place on the territory of Poland," Tusk told a televised press conference in Warsaw.
Thousands of European troops are taking part in military exercises in southeastern Poland. 
"Nobody can say that this was an innocent coincidence," Tusk said, adding he had informed NATO "straight away." 
Tusk said that NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte would be in Warsaw on Saturday and that he would inform him of the incident. 
Poland is one of five countries Europe picked to represent it at future US-led talks on Ukraine.  
 
- Bridge retaliation -
 
Russia, which has refused a ceasefire, has increased its strikes as temperatures dip in Ukraine, with many fearing this winter could be the worst of the war yet.   
Kyiv's state energy operator reported "significant damage" to the country's energy infrastructure that had "seriously impacted the operation of the power grid".
The Black Sea port city of Odesa was in a "critical" situation with a "widespread power outage", it said -- adding blackouts were also recorded in Kyiv and ten other regions.
Russia's military on Friday confirmed it had launched a "massive" attack with missiles and drones, saying they targeted military-industrial sites and transport infrastructure in several regions, including bridges in Kyiv.    
The UN has reported rising civilian casualties this year as Russia intensifies its long-range strikes.
UNICEF on Friday said at least 114 children had been killed and 1,030 wounded in the first 10 months of 2026 -- "a higher number of verified child casualties than in any of the past three years." 
"That is on average of more than three children killed or injured every single day," the organisation said, warning of an "alarming escalation in violence affecting children in Ukraine."  
US-led talks on ending the fighting have so far shown little signs of progress, with Moscow having stuck to its hardline demands.
Putin has said a deal to end the war in Ukraine must be part of a wider agreement on European security.
Speaking in China on Thursday, he said any form of Ukraine-Europe military cooperation as part of that deal would be a "problem".

title: Jeff Bezos Has Worked With 5 Presidents and Still Turns to Obama for Advice, Says Trump Is the Most Accessible of Them All — 'He'll Call You'
description:
Everyone needs a good sounding board. It helps when that sounding board used to live in the White House.
Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) founder Jeff Bezos still turns to former President Barack Obama for advice, but he says President Donald Trump beats every other president he has worked with when it comes to picking up the phone.
“I’ve worked with every president since Clinton, and I hope to work with every president going forward as long as they’ll have me,” Bezos said on Tuesday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference in Menlo Park, California. “Trump is particularly communicative. He reaches out a lot.”
“Clinton and Bush and Obama—Obama was very communicative too, and I still reach out to Obama for advice,” he continued. “He’s given me some good advice over the years.”
Trump Wins on Sheer Volume
Obama may have the advice, but Trump has the call log.
“But none of them were half as communicative as Trump is,” Bezos said. “Trump is the most accessible. You can call him, he’ll call you.”
“So he’s very unusual in that—not in terms of like qualitatively unusual, just quantitatively,” he continued. “Just the amount of outreach is unusual.”
Bezos said he doesn’t know who the next president will be or how much advice that person will want. “But I don’t think reaching out to the president or vice versa is a bad thing,” he said. “I think it’s a good thing, and most presidents do it to one degree or another.”
Bezos covered plenty of ground at the event, including his role in casting Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond.
Not Everyone Has a President on Speed Dial
Politics aside, the point is hard to miss. Whether someone cheers or groans at Bezos’ White House ties, staying in touch tends to pay off.
That kind of access isn’t on the table for the average worker, though, and plenty of Americans may feel shut out of conversations happening at that level.
The Rolodex Earns Its Keep
The lesson scales down, too. Bezos has shared plenty of advice for founders over the years, and he has praised politicians when he thinks they get policy right. A CEO who keeps in touch with investors and employees has an easier time when things get rocky, and the same goes for anyone building a career.
Voicemail has never closed a deal. Bezos still gets advice from Obama and calls from Trump, and he said he hopes people see that outreach “in the right light.”
Photo via Shutterstock

title: Hyperliquid Monero Crashes? Wagyu-Linked XMR1 Collapses, $13.2M Flows Into Ethereum
description:
Wagyu XMR1 Monero crashes 99% in Hyperliquid, 5.2 million tokens move from its deployer account, with $13.2 million converted into ETH.
The post Hyperliquid Monero Crashes? Wagyu-Linked XMR1 Collapses, $13.2M Flows Into Ethereum appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
A Monero token crashed 99% on Friday after 5.2 million XMR1 tokens moved from a wallet tied to its creator, triggering a massive sell-off on Hyperliquid. The token, issued through crypto swap service Wagyu, plunged from around $494 to below $1 in 35 minutes. The wallet receiving the tokens sold enough to generate $13.22 million in USDC before converting the proceeds into 7,467 ETH.

Wagyu’s wallet security and the backing behind its wrapped Monero product are being questioned. And the sell-off also sent shockwaves through the Monero market, although native XMR remained a separate asset from the collapsing XMR1 market.

Wagyu-Linked Wallet Moves 5.2 Million XMR1 Before Crash

The incident began this morning when the account responsible for deploying XMR1 transferred tokens to a newly created wallet. Blockchain intelligence firm Bitquery identified three separate transfers between 04:46 and 05:16 UTC. Two transactions moved 100,000 XMR1 each, followed by a much larger transfer of 5 million tokens.

The receiving wallet had been created that morning. It began selling shortly after receiving the tokens, overwhelming buyers on Hyperliquid’s order book. XMR1 had traded near $500 throughout the previous week. Its price then collapsed to $1 within 30 minutes, leaving holders with almost nothing.

Bitquery traced 363,804 tokens sold for $13.5 million. The remaining 4.83 million tokens stayed in the receiving wallet during its investigation. The sell-off also exposed how concentrated XMR1’s supply had been. Before the transfers, its deployer account still controlled 93% of the token’s supply.

Hyperliquid transfers require signatures from the account’s own key, rather than an ordinary trading API wallet. This means whoever authorized the transfers likely had access to the deployer’s main key. Whether someone stole that access or used it legitimately remains unknown.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

388 Buyers Pay $13.5 Million as Proceeds Move Into Ethereum

The damage extended beyond traders watching XMR1 collapse on their screens. It matched the seller’s transactions against 388 accounts that purchased the dumped tokens. One buyer alone paid $3.56 million, while 27 large buyers accounted for 77% of the total proceeds.

The wallet did not leave the money sitting in USDC. It began moving funds through Hyperliquid’s bridge into Arbitrum shortly after selling.

On Arbitrum, the wallet exchanged $13.22 million in USDC for 7,467 ETH through CoW Protocol. It then routed much of the Ethereum through Socket, Mayan, and Stargate. 6,810 ETH then arrived on Ethereum after those bridge transactions. Approximately 4,836 ETH landed in a newly created wallet that had not sent any funds onward.

The investigation also identified 7,348 ETH across three wallets during its tracking window. That left a substantial amount of the proceeds sitting outside the original trading account.

Native Monero Avoids Collapse as Wagyu and Hyperliquid Face Security Questions

Monero (XMR)
24h7d30d1yAll time

The incident has put Wagyu’s bridge infrastructure under scrutiny. XMR1 itself is Monero on Hyperliquid, but through Wagyu’s bridging service. Users can move native XMR into the service and receive XMR1 for trading. They can also reverse the process to recover their Monero.

Native XMR did not suffer the same collapse. Monero continued trading around $470–$482, while XMR1 lost virtually all its market value.

Holders now face a difficult question: Can they still exchange their remaining XMR1 for native Monero?

The incident also comes weeks after Wagyu disclosed a separate data leak on October 28. Researchers identified exposed records potentially linking crypto deposits, Monero receiving addresses, and customer IP addresses.

Wagyu previously said customer funds remained unaffected by that incident. No established connection links the October leak to Friday’s wallet transfers.

The latest investigation also uncovered another potential concern. The same deployer account controls 99.97% of ZEC1, a separate token representing Zcash on Hyperliquid.

title: Procter & Gamble Plans up to 30% Supply Job Cuts by 2030, Aims for $10 Billion in Cost Savings
description:
Procter & Gamble Company (NYSE:PG) stock edged slightly higher during Friday’s premarket session after closing roughly 1.4% lower after the consumer goods giant’s investor day event held on Thursday.
The company targets up to $10 billion in productivity savings between fiscal 2027 and 2030, building on savings of $2.8 billion in fiscal 2026.
The initiative comes as P&G faces mounting pressure from higher raw material, energy and freight costs, which are expected to weigh on annual profitability despite resilient demand for its beauty and home-care products.
The company in October reported better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter results and affirmed its fiscal 2027 organic sales and earnings guidance.
Organic sales increased 4% year over year, driven by volume, favorable product mix and a modest benefit from pricing.
However, core gross margin narrowed 150 basis points from a year earlier, impacted by higher commodity costs, product reinvestments and an unfavorable product mix.
Workforce Reduction And Supply Chain Efficiency
P&G plans to reduce its product-supply workforce, including contractors, by 20% to 30% by 2030, as part of its broader productivity and automation strategy.
Chief Financial Officer Andre Schulten noted that the plan includes up to $1.8 billion in annual productivity savings through cost-of-goods-sold improvements, Reuters reported.
The company is also expanding automation and digital capabilities across its supply chain to improve operational efficiency and control costs.
Outlook
P&G highlighted improving sales momentum, with organic revenue growth expected to reach approximately 3% in the first half of fiscal 2027, compared with 2% in the second half of fiscal 2026.
For fiscal 2027, the company maintained its organic sales growth outlook of 1% to 3% and net sales growth forecast of 2% to 4%.
The company expects approximately $2 billion in pretax restructuring costs over two years, with more than half incurred in fiscal 2026 and the remainder expected in fiscal 2027.
PG Price Action: Procter & Gamble shares were up 1.17% at $169.81 during premarket trading on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.
Image via Shutterstock

title: Crypto Price Analysis Nov-20: ETH, XRP, ADA, BNB, and HYPE
description: Today, we examine Ethereum, Ripple, Cardano, Binance Coin, and Hyperliquid in greater detail. Ethereum (ETH) In a major move, Ethereum has lost its support at $1,800 as it closes the week 9% lower. This opens the way for the price to fall all the way to $1,500, which is a critical level not tested since […]
fullContent:
Today, we examine Ethereum, Ripple, Cardano, Binance Coin, and Hyperliquid in greater detail.

Ethereum (ETH)

In a major move, Ethereum has lost its support at $1,800 as it closes the week 9% lower. This opens the way for the price to fall all the way to $1,500, which is a critical level not tested since June 2026.

If nothing changes by Sunday, this will be the seventh consecutive weekly candle closing in red, something we have not seen since the bear market from 2022. If this is a repeat of that, lower lows are likely.

Looking ahead, best to prepare mentally for a re-test of $1,500. Any failure there and this cryptocurrency will likely approach $1,300 or even $1,000 after that. A more optimistic scenario would be a relief rally around $1,500.

Ripple (XRP)

XRP fell by 6% this week as the price continued to struggle under the $1 resistance. With buyers unable to reclaim that key psychological level, this cryptocurrency has only one way left to go, down.

The most important support level on the chart is found at $0.70. However, before XRP tests it, buyers could attempt a relief rally to give bears a break from their nonstop assault on the price.

Looking ahead, XRP’s only chance to recover is to reclaim $1 as support, where it needs to form a strong base. Anything less than that would see the price continue its descent towards $0.70.

Cardano (ADA)

After a promising summer, ADA has returned on the $0.15 level, erasing all its progress this year. Worse, it closes the week 12% lower with no sign of stopping. This puts sellers firmly in charge and only a lower price level may satisfy them.

With no relief in sight, the most important support level under $0.15 is found at $0.10. While a direct drop to that level seems unlikely, expect this level to be tested if sellers retain the upper hand in the future.

Looking ahead, Cardano is found in a dire position. Its price seems ready for new yearly lows, which would reopen the race towards searching for a bottom, as the previous low from June 2026 appears to have been just a temporary relief.

Binance Coin (BNB)

Binance Coin continues to suffer after the Binance hack. The price is now 30% lower than its peak from October and also turned $580 into a resistance. With bears in control, BNB also closed the week 9% lower.

Since buyers are absent, this cryptocurrency will have to seek lower levels to attract them. The most likely candidate is $500. Such a price would entail a lower low, even below the June low at around $540.

Looking ahead, the outlook remains bearish as the aftermath of the Binance hack continues to impact BNB. It’s likely that any bullish reversal will have to wait and may return only in 2027.

Hype (HYPE)

Hyperliquid is down 9% on the weekly timeframe after its price fell below its bearish wedge, a formation that has highlighted a bearish bias for several months now. With this drop, HYPE is likely to remain bearish in the coming months.

The first target for sellers will be found around $50. That level should attract buyers as it would entail almost a 50% drop from its current all-time high at $98. Still, after such an aggressive bull run for most of 2026, a correction of 50% would be quite shallow in crypto terms.

Looking ahead, Hyperliquid will remain in a downtrend and will struggle to find support, especially if the overall crypto market remains bearish in the coming months. While a relief rally seems unlikely now, watch the reaction at $50 closely, as it is a strong candidate for a bounce.

The post Peter Brandt Points to a 75% Bitcoin Correction Pattern. Will the Crash Deepen? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Veteran trader Peter Brandt has flagged a pattern that has repeated throughout Bitcoin’s history. According to him, every major bull market ended with a correction of at least 75%.

With Bitcoin already well below its peak, traders now wonder whether history could repeat itself.

Peter Brandt Spots a Recurring Bitcoin Pattern

Veteran trader Peter Brandt, who has analyzed markets for five decades, shared the observation on X.

According to him, every major Bitcoin bull market has ended with a correction of at least 75% from its parabolic peak. To support his view, he posted a long-term weekly chart of BTC/USD.

The chart shows successive parabolic rallies, each followed by a sharp decline. It also tracks volume data and measures the time span of each cycle.

Moreover, one annotation points to a 70% retracement level near $37,629. For now, Bitcoin trades at $61,650, roughly 51% below its October 2025 peak. If the pattern repeats from that peak, a 75% drop would point to roughly $31,500.

Early Bitcoin rallies often ended with drops of 80% to 90% or more. Although later cycles brought milder declines, Brandt stresses that a 75% minimum retracement has held so far.

Is Bitcoin Headed for a 75% Crash?

Not necessarily. Brandt’s post serves as a reminder of Bitcoin’s historical behavior, not a prediction of an imminent collapse.

Still, the debate has intensified. Many traders question whether the current pullback marks the start of a deeper correction or something milder.

Other prominent voices have also weighed in. Crypto Rover, who has over 1.6 million followers on X, said Bitcoin could crash to $55,000 this year after breaking support. That level would mean a further drop of roughly 11% from current prices.

In contrast, Michael Saylor remained constructive. In an investor Q&A shared on November 20, he discussed buying Bitcoin and managing risk through a prolonged downturn.

He also covered funding dividends and creating long-term shareholder value. As a result, his comments reinforced a continued accumulation strategy. Saylor’s Strategy remains the largest corporate Bitcoin holder.

For now, traders following classical charts see Brandt’s post as a cautionary reference. Ultimately, the market itself will decide whether this cycle produces a correction of that scale.

title: U.S. and Israel reportedly weigh new attack on Iran that could come within days
description:
Tel Aviv — Israel and the U.S. are considering launching a new assault on Iran in the short term, according to sources familiar with the matter. 
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's administration is concerned about how rapidly the Iranians are rebuilding their ballistic missile manufacturing capabilities and the pace at which Iran is working to shield its military and nuclear infrastructure from attack by moving it underground, the sources told CBS News.
President Trump also said this week that Iran may be seeking to develop chemical or biological weapons, though he provided no evidence to support the claim.
Months of indirect negotiations between the U.S. and Iran have failed to bring a ceasefire deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran has refused to even discuss its nuclear program unless the U.S. lifts its naval blockade and accepts six other key conditions. 
Israel's military is prepared for a new round of fighting with Iran and is in peak defensive posture to respond to any first attack by Iran, the sources told CBS News. 
The Netanyahu administration would prefer to launch a new joint operation with the U.S., but the sources told CBS News it remains unclear whether Mr. Trump wants to order new military action, and if so, what kind. The war was a key factor in the Republicans' defeat in the recent midterm elections and it remains deeply unpopular with Americans. 
The U.S. has significant firepower in the region, including tens of thousands of forces and two aircraft carriers with their associated strike groups, amounting to dozens of warships and aircraft.
For both Mr. Trump and Netanyahu, who jointly launched the war with Iran almost nine months ago with a massive round of strikes on the Islamic Republic, the window for any new collaborative action may be closing.

Netanyahu could lose his position as prime minister in the coming weeks due to the results of Israel's national election late last month. Mr. Trump's Republican party will lose control of both houses of the U.S. Congress in January, meanwhile, giving his political opponents far greater say over financing of the war. 
Neither Netanyahu's office nor Israel's military responded to CBS News' requests for comment on the planning for any renewed attacks on Iran, which would be the third round of major hostilities. The White House and U.S. military declined to comment on the current thinking within the administration, but American military commanders have long said they are prepared to execute any orders Mr. Trump gives. With the assets already in place a new offensive operation could be mounted within two to four days, if such an order were given.
Mr. Trump has said repeatedly that Iran is keen to make a deal to end the war, but Tehran has rejected any ceasefire to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, or any talks on its nuclear program, unless the U.S. agrees to seven key demands, including an end to hostilities on all fronts in the Middle East and an end of the U.S. blockade of Iran's ports and vessels. 
Alongside the rising concern over Iran's growing capacity to produce conventional weapons — which the regime has boasted of itself —   President Trump also raised the possibility of the Islamic Republic working to obtain biological or chemical weapons.
"They're looking at gases, looking at bio, because we've shut them out with the nuclear," Mr. Trump told a Fox News reporter in China ahead of his meeting with his Russian and Chinese counterparts.
Iran's foreign ministry rejected the allegations on Thursday, comparing it to U.S. claims that Iraq was developing weapons of mass destruction before the invasion launched by then-President George W. Bush in 2003. 
"We find ourselves facing ominous new allegations and a narrative that appears to be following the same fraudulent script," Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said in a post on X. 
President Trump has offered no clear signal about whether he intends to order major new military action against Iran. He told Fox News on Wednesday that he still wanted to reach a deal with Iran, but one that he feels will last, and also renewed his threat to use force.
"I'm going to finish it off," Mr. Trump said of the war. "Yeah, soon. I mean, one way or the other, we'll finish it off."
On Thursday, however, he told Israel's Channel 12 that he's "not rushing into any decision," indicating a willingness, not for the first time, to let the stalemate drag on into 2027.
"We will see what happens after the beginning of the year," he told the television network.
U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper, who oversees American forces in the Middle East, met with top Israeli security officials at Israel's defense ministry Wednesday for what the Israeli military called a "joint, comprehensive situational assessment."
Israel's most senior general, Eyal Zamir, as well as the director of the Mossad intelligence agency, Roman Gofman, were among the senior Israeli officials who met with Cooper.
Israeli authorities confirming the Mossad director's attendance at the meeting was unusual, and many in the country have taken it as a sign that Iran was a key topic of discussion. 
Gofman met U.S. officials in Washington last week, including CIA Director John Ratcliffe, according to people familiar with the matter.
"The head of the Mossad, who hardly leaves the country, didn't go for a brief in and out, but for a couple of days. It's a serious matter on the table," said Erez Winner, chairman of the Israel Defense and Security Forum, an Israeli think tank with close ties to the Netanyahu administration.
If the decision is made to take Israel back to war with Iran, it would come at a politically sensitive time for Netanyahu. 
His political rivals, in the wake of last month's election, have been tasked with forming a government, potentially leaving him in power for just a few more weeks, possibly less. 
Since losing his majority in Israel's parliament, Netanyahu has made the argument to his rivals, and to the Israeli public, that a unity government is required to deal with the country's pressing security threats. He has long accused Iran of having ambitions to build nuclear weapons, and placed that at the pinnacle of those threats.
Iran has always denied any desire to build nuclear weapons, though after President Trump pulled the U.S. out of a previous international nuclear agreement during his first term, it has enriched uranium to a point far beyond the needs of civilian nuclear programs. 
International monitors believe Iran still has a stockpile of about 900 pounds of uranium enriched to 60% purity somewhere under the rubble of its heavily damaged nuclear facilities. At that level, the material is just a short technological step away from being enriched to weapons-grade. 
Despite the concerns, some of Netanyahu's political rivals believe he is trying to take the country back to war to avoid losing power. In recent days, he has held security briefings with some of those rivals — an unusual step that analysts say may hint at the possibility of imminent military action.
President Trump endorsed Netanyahu before the Israeli election, and he said he also would prefer to pair up with the right-wing Israeli leader in any new attack on Iran.
The speculation about a major new operation comes amid a renewed tit-for-tat exchange of fire between Iran and the U.S.
The U.S. launched a strike on Iran's strategic Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, which American officials categorized as self-defense in response to Iranian strikes targeting U.S. assets in Bahrain, which the U.S. military said were intercepted. Iran has also launched strikes against Kuwait this week, with officials saying they caused no damage.

The Iranian regime has been preparing, publicly, for renewed hostilities, and it has warned that its response to any new attack would reach farther than its previous actions.
Iranian government and military officials, including senior members of the powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, have threatened to widen retaliatory attacks to target not just Israel and U.S. military infrastructure in Persian Gulf states, but U.S. bases in Europe, Gulf energy infrastructure and undersea internet cables. 
A recent statement attributed to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said in the event of a return to open hostilities, "there would be no geographical limit for Iranian missiles."  
This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/iran-war-us-israel-considering-new-assault-sources-say/

title: EU Warns Spain, Czechia on Crypto Tax Data
description:
Summary Commission escalated both DAC8 cases to reasoned opinions Czech DAC8 bill still awaits final approval Foreign platforms still report […]
The post EU Warns Spain, Czechia on Crypto Tax Data appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Summary

  • Commission escalated both DAC8 cases to reasoned opinions
  • Czech DAC8 bill still awaits final approval
  • Foreign platforms still report Spanish and Czech residents
  • Reported totals are not the same as gains

The European Commission sent reasoned opinions to both countries on November 19, the second formal step in its infringement procedure over DAC8, the EU directive that makes crypto platforms report customer activity to tax authorities.

Twelve countries were warned in January; two were escalated

The Commission sent letters of formal notice to twelve member states in January for failing to bring DAC8 into national law on time. Spain and Czechia are the two it has now moved to the next stage, stating that both still fail to fully implement the directive.

A reasoned opinion is the Commission’s formal finding that a country is breaching EU law. Each government now has two months to respond and adopt the missing measures. If they don’t, the Commission can refer the cases to the Court of Justice of the European Union and ask for financial sanctions. Under the EU treaties, a country that fails to notify how it has transposed a directive can face fines in the first court ruling, without the second round of proceedings usually required.

The deadline applies to governments. Investors in either country have nothing to file because of it.

Two countries, two different delays

Spain is not starting from zero. Crypto providers based there already file information returns with the tax agency, covering balances and transactions under forms 172 and 173. The government sent its DAC8 bill to parliament in June 2025, and the finance ministry published a draft royal decree a month later to set out the due-diligence and reporting detail. Seventeen months after the bill went to parliament, Brussels still considers the job unfinished.

Czechia has further to go. The government sent its bill to the Chamber of Deputies on February 5, 2026, after the directive’s January 1 deadline had already passed, as the finance minister told deputies. In October, the Chamber’s bill record listed it at second reading. It still needs a final vote, Senate approval and the president’s signature. The Czech Financial Administration has treated 2026 as the first reporting year regardless, but providers still have no adopted law to report under.

The Commission’s announcement does not list which provisions each country is missing.

Why the gap sits on the outgoing side

DAC8 assigns reporting to the country where a platform is authorised, not the country where its customer lives. That design determines which flows the Spanish and Czech delays can disrupt.

Inbound: largely unaffected

A Spanish resident trades on a platform authorised in Ireland. The platform reports to Ireland’s Revenue, which passes the data to Spain under existing automatic-exchange arrangements. Ireland has transposed DAC8, so Spain’s unfinished law does not stop this flow.

Outbound: where the uncertainty is

A German resident trades on a platform authorised in Spain or Czechia. That platform owes its DAC8 report to Madrid or Prague. Without complete national rules, its legal duty to collect tax residence details and report is less certain. So is the data Germany expects to receive.

That’s why delays in two countries are an EU-wide problem. Every other member state counts on Spanish and Czech authorities to send data about its residents.

The coverage also extends beyond EU platforms. DAC8 is the EU’s version of the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, and the directive requires operators from outside the EU that serve EU customers without authorisation under MiCA, the EU’s crypto-markets regulation, to register in one member state and report there.

The DAC8 calendar

  1. January 1, 2026 – first year of reportable crypto activity begins
  2. January 2026 – formal notices to twelve member states
  3. November 19, 2026 – reasoned opinions to Spain and Czechia
  4. Mid-January 2027 – two-month response window closes
  5. May 31, 2027 – filing deadline for Irish-authorised providers; other countries set their own
  6. September 30, 2027 – first exchanges of 2026 data between EU tax authorities, per the Commission

A €10,000 report, a €2,000 gain

When the data arrives, it comes as totals. Revenue’s reporting guidance lists the fields: the customer’s name, address, tax residence and tax identification number, plus aggregate amounts, units and transaction counts for each crypto-asset, split by purchases, sales and transfers.

Take an investor who bought Bitcoin for €8,000 and sold it for €10,000. The report shows €10,000 of gross sale proceeds. The gain is €2,000 before fees. If the purchase was made on a different platform, possibly years before DAC8 existed, the selling platform has no record of the €8,000 cost. The tax authority sees the larger number unless the investor supplies the smaller one.

The directive leaves the tax itself to each country. Coindoo’s look at Greece’s proposed 10% rate and €500 exemption shows the choices national governments still make on rates, cost basis and losses. A DAC8 report feeds those rules but replaces none of them.

READ MORE:

Is Bitcoin Dead? Jack Mallers Points to Its History

Wallet withdrawals leave a trace, not a trail

Moving coins into self-custody does not remove them from the report. The directive requires platforms to report the aggregate value and units of transfers to blockchain addresses not known to belong to another crypto provider or financial institution.

The record stops at the withdrawal. DAC8 does not follow coins after they leave the platform, establish who controls the receiving address, or give authorities access to private keys. A withdrawal to an investor’s own hardware wallet and a payment to a stranger can therefore look the same in the report. Only the investor’s records show which one it was.

Records that explain a reported transfer

  • Purchase confirmations showing price paid and fees
  • Withdrawal transaction IDs matched to the receiving deposit
  • A list of the wallet addresses you control
  • Annual statements from every platform you used

The UK’s tax authority deals with the same reconciliation problem under its own rules, as Coindoo’s UK crypto tax explainer shows.

What to watch in January

By mid-January, Spain and Czechia must either tell the Commission their transposition is complete or risk a referral to the EU Court of Justice. For Czechia, that depends on the bill clearing both chambers in time. For Spain, it depends on finishing both the law and the royal decree that puts it into practice.

Investors in both countries are already covered on the inbound side by every platform authorised elsewhere in the EU. What remains open is how fully Spanish and Czech platforms will report their 2026 activity, and what Madrid and Prague can send to the rest of the bloc when the first exchanges are due.

title: Michael Saylor Explains When Strategy Buys Bitcoin — And Why It Sometimes Chooses STRC Instead
description: Michael Saylor has offered a closer look at how Strategy decides between buying more Bitcoin and repurchasing its preferred shares, revealing a capital allocation approach that goes beyond accumulating BTC whenever prices fall. In a November 20 post on X, the Strategy executive chairman shared highlights from the company’s latest investor Q&A, featuring CEO Phong […]
fullContent:
Michael Saylor has offered a closer look at how Strategy decides between buying more Bitcoin and repurchasing its preferred shares, revealing a capital allocation approach that goes beyond accumulating BTC whenever prices fall.

In a November 20 post on X, the Strategy executive chairman shared highlights from the company’s latest investor Q&A, featuring CEO Phong Le and host Natalie Brunell. The discussion addressed Bitcoin per share, shareholder value, preferred-stock repurchases, and the company’s ability to meet financial obligations during prolonged market downturns.

The timing is particularly interesting. As institutional Bitcoin exposure continues to attract attention, Strategy is demonstrating that managing its financial obligations can be just as important as expanding its Bitcoin treasury.

How do we decide when to buy Bitcoin and when to buy back $STRC?

Why Strategy Sometimes Chooses STRC Over Bitcoin

During the investor discussion, Saylor and Le examined the conditions under which Strategy issues equity, purchases Bitcoin, or repurchases STRC, its variable-rate preferred stock.

The distinction matters because each transaction serves a different purpose.

Purchasing Bitcoin expands Strategy’s exposure to the digital asset. Repurchasing STRC, particularly when shares trade below their $100 stated amount, can reduce outstanding preferred obligations and improve the company’s financial flexibility.

Strategy’s latest disclosures illustrate the difference.

Between November 9 and November 15, the company purchased 485 BTC while spending approximately $228.1 million repurchasing STRC shares. The Bitcoin acquisition cost roughly $33.4 million.

That means Strategy allocated substantially more capital to preferred-stock repurchases than direct Bitcoin purchases during that reporting period.

However, this does not necessarily indicate declining confidence in Bitcoin. Instead, the company appears to be balancing long-term BTC accumulation with the financial structure supporting that strategy.

Similar questions about corporate Bitcoin holdings have become increasingly relevant as investors examine how companies manage their digital asset treasuries.

Michael Saylor Highlights Bitcoin Per Share

Another important topic from the November 20 discussion was Bitcoin per share, a metric Strategy uses to evaluate how its financing decisions affect shareholders.

Saylor distinguished between gross and net Bitcoin per share, explaining why investors with different time horizons may interpret the measures differently.

Gross Bitcoin per share reflects the company’s Bitcoin exposure relative to its assumed diluted share base, while net Bitcoin per share accounts for relevant financial claims and liabilities.

The broader question is whether Strategy can increase the economic value attributable to shareholders through its capital-market activities, rather than relying entirely on Bitcoin price appreciation.

This is particularly relevant when the company issues new shares to finance acquisitions or repurchases.

Although additional Bitcoin purchases can increase total holdings, issuing equity also changes the ownership denominator. As a result, the number of BTC held by Strategy is not the only metric investors should monitor.

Growing institutional Bitcoin positions reinforce the importance of understanding how different financial structures provide exposure to BTC.

Can Strategy Keep Buying Bitcoin During A Downturn?

Strategy’s financial resilience was another central theme of the Q&A.

According to its latest reporting, the company held 850,849 BTC as of November 15, alongside approximately $4.9 billion in US dollar assets.

Its dollar reserves and other liquid assets are intended to help support preferred dividends, debt obligations, and broader treasury management.

The company has also reported approximately 3.4 years of coverage for interest and dividend obligations at prevailing rates.

These financial considerations are detailed in Strategy’s official third-quarter 2026 financial results, which provide additional context for its Bitcoin treasury and capital-market activities.

That liquidity provides a buffer against prolonged Bitcoin weakness, although future financing conditions, dividend rates, and market volatility remain important considerations.

For Bitcoin investors, the central takeaway is that Strategy’s accumulation model is becoming more sophisticated.

Rather than treating every available dollar as an automatic Bitcoin purchase, management is weighing the benefits of increasing BTC holdings against strengthening the financial instruments that support those holdings.

Saylor’s latest remarks suggest that Strategy still sees Bitcoin as its core long-term asset, while capital management is playing an increasingly important role in determining how the company expands its exposure.

title: GTA 6 Crypto Token Looked Like a Launch-Day Hit: Who Was Really Buying?
description:
A GTA 6 crypto token drew 3,903 SOL in its first hour. BitOK traced 95% of that buying to its own creator.
The post GTA 6 Crypto Token Looked Like a Launch-Day Hit: Who Was Really Buying? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Nearly 95% of a GTA 6 crypto token’s first-hour buying came from wallets tied to its creator, according to a blockchain analytics report from BitOK shared with BeInCrypto exclusively. Outside buyers put in about 201 SOL and lost a quarter of it.

The token, Grand Theft Alleycat, launched on Thursday, Nov. 19, the day Rockstar Games set for the game’s release. Traders chasing that hype were the target, because staged volume made the token look in demand.

How the Fake Demand Was Built

The token was created on pump.fun, a site for launching Solana tokens in minutes. Buyers pay in SOL, Solana’s native coin.

In the first hour, purchases reached 3,903 SOL. BitOK traced 3,454.8 SOL of that to 1,265 wallets funded by a single operator-controlled hub before they bought.

None of them sold. With the launch wallets and five other operator accounts added, nearly 95% of buying was the operator’s own.

Nineteen wallets that bought the token at creation sold it for 3,202.8 SOL. BitOK says the operator was selling the token to itself.

The hub sent 10,795.5 SOL to a treasury wallet. That wallet held 3,856.24 SOL on Nov. 20, a balance BeInCrypto confirmed on-chain.

Why Losses Look Small but the Scheme Keeps Running

BitOK links the same operator to GTA6DOG (RICO), an Ethereum token whose code let its creator pull tokens from any wallet without permission. From Nov. 3 to 5, it emptied 10 buyers.

BitOK puts outside losses across both tokens at a preliminary $4,746. For Grand Theft Alleycat, that counts only the first hour of trading.

After that first hour, the price collapsed. GeckoTerminal data shows the token fell about 99.8% from its peak of roughly $0.001 and has barely traded since.

The trail runs through US exchanges. Network fees for the launches were paid with withdrawals from Coinbase and Kraken, alongside Bitget and SideShift. Another 41.99 ETH reached the HitBTC exchange.

No authority has charged anyone. BitOK, which sells address screening to exchanges and police, based its findings on wallet transfers.

GTA-themed tokens have burned traders before. The CYBERLEEK leak coin fell nearly 60% in August after its biggest spoiler.

On Nov. 20, the same signing keys launched two more tokens, Anthropic Cat Brian and iCat.

In May, South Korean prosecutors charged five people over a Solana meme coin rug pull.

The post GTA 6 Crypto Token Looked Like a Launch-Day Hit: Who Was Really Buying? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Two New Ways to Borrow Against Bitcoin
description:
DeFi lender Aave voted on 9 November to add a market where users can lock native bitcoin and borrow USDt and other stablecoins on Ethereum. The incoming vault keeps coins…
The post Two New Ways to Borrow Against Bitcoin appeared first on Bitfinex blog.
fullContent:
DeFi lender Aave voted on 9 November to add a market where users can lock native bitcoin and borrow USDt and other stablecoins on Ethereum. The incoming vault keeps coins on the Bitcoin network locked in a vault with no custodian.

The technology comes from bitcoin infrastructure provider Babylon, which calls the product Trustless Bitcoin Vaults. Babylon says it aims to launch late 2026, starting with a restricted phase that limits users and volume. Aave’s DAO vote drew 76 voters carrying about 357,000 AAVE tokens of voting power with none opposed.

Institutions Get a Regulated Custodial Route

Soon after, on 16 November, crypto lender Abra announced dollar loans to institutions against bitcoin, ether and solana in partnership with Intercontinental Exchange, owner of the New York Stock Exchange. The coins are deposited to a segregated wallet at ICE Digital Trust, a trust company chartered in New York. They are not re-pledged or lent on and leave only under controls agreed by borrower, lender and custodian.

“Historically, borrowing against Bitcoin meant trusting your lender with the asset. That model is done,” said Bill Barhydt, Founder and CEO of Abra. “With ICE Digital Trust, the collateral sits with a qualified custodian. … This is what digital assets for institutions are supposed to look like.”

The two products are evidence of the crypto market’s increasing sophistication as teams develop products tailored to the needs of institutional and individual investors. For the former, fully regulated solutions are rolling out in partnership with professional custodians, and, for those staying true to the self-custody ethos, decentralised markets are improving their own custody models. 

Lending Recovers While Custody Models Diverge

Crypto lending has already been through one collapse and recovery. After peaking in 2021 at $69.37 billion, the market plunged in 2022 after the bankruptcies of centralised lenders like Celsius and BlockFi, which had engaged in opaque and risky lending practices.  

Galaxy Research noted in a report released in August 2026 that a new peak was reached in crypto-backed lending in the third quarter of 2025, of $78.69 billion in loans, however since then the market has declined reaching $56.16 billion by June 2026.

Tether, the largest centralised lender in Galaxy’s tally, reported $14.18 billion of secured loans at the end of September, up from $13.45 billion in June. Onchain and centralised lenders are close in size. Galaxy puts on-chain venues at 59 percent of crypto-backed lending at the end of June and centralised lenders at 41 percent.

ICE and Abra offer institutions a regulated custodian, a credit approval and a written contract. Abra says it and its predecessors have facilitated more than $2 billion of digital asset loans since 2021. Naturally, the borrower must depend on a third party to reliably fulfil its obligations.

On the new Aave market, a depositor locks BTC in a Taproot UTXO on the Bitcoin network — a type of transaction output which applies programmable rules to an amount of unspent bitcoin. “Redemption is governed by on-chain rules (e.g., the depositor repaid their loan) and settles directly to a Bitcoin UTXO controlled by the redeeming party,” according to Babylon. 

Once everyone has signed, the owner activates the vault. The coins stay on Bitcoin. A matching record appears on Ethereum, and it is erased when the vault is withdrawn or liquidated.

However, people are still involved. An approved group of arbitrageurs settle liquidations. Two groups of signers using a 4-of-7 and a 3-of-5 multisig sit over Babylon’s contracts and can pause them at once, which shuts the exits. 

These human interventions can prove useful in the case of bad actors attempting to break the system. While none of these parties holds the coins or can move them individually, there is a certain amount of trust still at work. 

For bitcoin holders, the question has increasingly become which risk they want to be paid for. Borrowers now face the same choice. One model asks them to trust a regulated custodian and a contract. The other asks them to trust code and operators working within well-defined limits. 

Neither model requires them to trust the lender with the coins, which is what failed in 2022. The custodial version is open to institutions today and has the potential to offer a route to crypto lending traditional capital requires. Onchain solutions continue to innovate, however, and Babylon’s native bitcoin market on Aave has the potential to provide DeFi solutions to a new user base. 

The post Two New Ways to Borrow Against Bitcoin appeared first on Bitfinex blog.

title: Bitcoin tailspin continues: Where will it all end?
description: The Anthropic IPO launched into a downtrending stock market having sucked a lot of the value out of the rest of the AI sector and the tech market in general. Down on the day and in pre-market, an Anthropic sell-off could weigh heavily on an already falling market. Bitcoin is being dragged below its last levels of support. How far down can it go?
fullContent:
The Anthropic IPO launched into a downtrending stock market having sucked a lot of the value out of the rest of the AI sector and the tech market in general. Down on the day and in pre-market, an Anthropic sell-off could weigh heavily on an already falling market. Bitcoin is being dragged below its last levels of support. How far down can it go?

A continued descent to $60K

Source: TradingView

What the eye is drawn to in the short-term chart for $BTC is that the price is falling below major structural supports and there doesn’t seem to be an end in sight for this collapse. Falling below the bull market trendline is a huge blow for the Bitcoin bulls, but if the rot doesn’t stop soon, and the $BTC price falls below $57,700, Bitcoin would be back in its bear market. This would be almost unthinkable after such a strong rally up to $87K.

As things stand, the price is still bleeding out, and we could witness a descent to the $60K horizontal support level. From there, it’s not much further to the very depths of what most believe is the bear market bottom at $57,700. Is the $BTC price going to go there and recontinue the bear market?

The only cheer for the bulls is that bullish divergence has formed as the price has gone down while the RSI has risen. Also, the Stochastic RSI indicators are nearing their bottom and could signal a bounce going into the weekend.

Is Bitcoin about to reenter its bear market?

Source: TradingView

The daily chart is not a good look either. The $BTC price falling below the huge ascending channel is a bad omen, and this also puts paid to the chances of an inverse head and shoulders pattern, given that the right shoulder is now bigger than the head. 

The two support levels can be clearly seen below, with the lower of these absolutely critical for the new green shoots of a bull market. If the $BTC price goes below this, the bear market is back in force, and it then remains to be seen how deep it will go.

$57,700, or all the way down to $39K?

Source: TradingView

In the weekly time frame it can be seen that this week’s candle opened below the bull market trendline, and is the first one to do so, going all the way back to the end of 2022. Already looking as though it could put in a weekly break below the $62,600 support level, the $BTC price could be heading for the current bear market bottom of $57,700, which lines up nicely with the 0.618 Fibonacci level (taken from the very bottom of the previous bull market to its top). 

If there is going to be a bounce, it’s probably from this level, which makes perfect sense. Nonetheless, looking at this structure, a bounce could take the $BTC price back up to the bull market trendline to either confirm the breakdown, or to continue on into the new bull market. This could potentially be the last critical test for Bitcoin.

Then again, if $57,700 fails, a drop to $39K could be next. This is where the 0.786 Fibonacci level is to be found, and the drop could even coincide with a retest of the bear market trendline. This would equate to a total 69% bear market correction - much more in line with previous bear markets.

title: Was Anthropic’s IPO the Real Reason Behind Bitcoin’s November Crash?
description: More than a third of Bitcoin's drop came before November, and the heaviest week of ETF outflows came before Anthropic set its price range.
fullContent:
Bitcoin (BTC) traded below $64,000 on Thursday morning, the day Anthropic makes its Nasdaq debut, down from more than $87,000 in late September, CoinGecko data shows. Then, it dropped further to under $62,000.

More and more analysts, and even digital asset executives like Brad Garglinghouse have laid out the connection between Bitcoin’s November collapse and the AI giant IPO.

For instance, Crypto analyst Michaël van de Poppe blamed the listing, writing on X that some players had been selling Bitcoin to be ready for the IPO. He compared the move to BTC’s dip before SpaceX’s IPO in June. The asset fell almost 29% in the weeks before that listing, then recovered above $80,000.

Ripple’s CEO made a similar case about the IPO on CNBC on Thursday, saying investors were steering capital toward big public listings and away from crypto. Anthropic priced the listing at $83 a share on Wednesday, above its planned range of $70 to $78. The share sale raised $81.3 billion and values the company at about $1.5 trillion fully diluted, CNBC reported.

Timing Undercuts the Drain Theory

Bitcoin was already about $7,300 below its peak on October 26, the day Anthropic made its IPO filing public, CoinGecko data shows. That is close to 30% of the roughly $25,000 the asset lost between its September high and Wednesday’s low, by CryptoPotato’s count.

Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterms, and voters rejected data-center projects in 40 of 41 ballot measures, CNN reported. Two days after those midterms, Bitcoin posted the biggest one-day drop of its slide, losing about $5,000 to close near $75,700 on CoinGecko’s daily figures.

Anthropic set its price range on November 10. By then, US spot Bitcoin ETFs had lost about $1.28 billion in the first week of November, their heaviest week of outflows this month, CryptoPotato’s tally of Farside Investors data shows.

Bitcoin ended that week only about $1,900 lower, after a post-election rally to near $80,700 on November 4. The following week, outflows eased to about $1.07 billion, while BTC dropped more than $7,600.

The ETFs lost $1.5B during the second full week of November, as we reported. However, BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes said on van de Poppe’s podcast that he does not see the IPO as a liquidity drain. He called Thursday’s debut the bellwether for the whole story. He said a strong listing would lift risk assets, Bitcoin included, and a weak one would spell trouble for all of them.

The Feud Behind Nvidia’s Crisis

Social media posts have gone further, claiming Anthropic pushed Jensen Huang out as Nvidia’s chief executive. They lean on a long feud between the two companies over chip sales to China.

Huang had repeatedly pressed Trump for freedom to sell advanced chips in China. In December 2025, Trump allowed sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips there in exchange for a 25% cut, which Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei strongly opposed, attacking those H200 sales at the World Economic Forum in Davos the following month.

“I think this is crazy. It’s a bit like selling nuclear weapons to North Korea,” Amodei said.

Anthropic’s lobbying has been noticed. Continental Strategy has lobbied for Anthropic since April 2025, federal disclosures show.

Continental’s income from Anthropic rose from $90,000 in its first quarter on the account to $150,000 in each of the first three quarters of 2026. Its second-quarter 2026 report lists the National Security Council among the offices lobbied, and its third-quarter report lists the State Department, both of which Rubio oversees.

Rubio also oversaw a classified memo on Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore firm that bought billions of dollars of Nvidia chips. US intelligence suspects Alice Huang of working for Beijing, and China’s foreign ministry called that allegation groundless.

That memo circulated before Trump’s May 13 to 15 trip to China. Trump’s delegation for that trip, announced on May 11, did not include Huang, CNN reported. Trump phoned him the next day to invite him, and Rubio briefed Trump on the concerns during that afternoon’s flight to Anchorage. Huang boarded in Alaska for the final leg to Beijing.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s department began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 over possible export violations, though it never added the company to the Entity List, which is a US trade blacklist.

Lutnick was also sent Rubio’s memo, Axios reported, but now House Democrats are asking whether Cantor Fitzgerald’s holdings improperly influenced Lutnick’s decisions, considering his sons run the firm, which held around 3.5 million Nvidia shares, worth about $1.2 billion, when he was confirmed.

However, Cantor reduced its Nvidia position by nearly 50% just months before the the latter’s fiasco, now at 1.72 million.

At a Situation Room meeting on November 5, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pressed Lutnick on why Megaspeed was not blacklisted. Lutnick stammered that he did not know and would look into it, CNN reported, citing people familiar with the meeting.

Commerce spokesperson Kristen Eichamer told Axios: “This is false. Secretary Bessent and Secretary Lutnick had no such conversation.”

Lutnick also warned that day that export controls would start a trade war with China, according to Axios. That trade war flared in October 2025, when Trump’s announcement of a 100% tariff on Chinese tech exports set off crypto’s worst single-day liquidation, more than $19 billion in leveraged positions.

How the AI Trade Reaches Bitcoin

Nvidia’s board accepted Huang’s resignation as chief executive on November 11, when Bitcoin traded near $73,700. BTC lost about $10,300 over the next three days, the worst three-day stretch of its slide.

The heaviest loss came on Saturday, November 14, when US stock markets were closed and Bitcoin’s loss was about $4,700, taking it to $63,500. As reported, many feared that Nvidia’s crisis could spill further into Bitcoin if investors unwound the AI trade.

Nvidia had shed about $1 trillion in market value since late October, part of it after the midterms. CNN reported that Huang’s troubles stirred fears among lobbyists and policymakers that Congress would regulate AI companies more tightly, which could dampen the gains that have lifted the stock market.

BitMine Chairman Tom Lee laid out how that pressure reaches crypto in an October 19 press release. He said worries over AI funding and AI model safety had set off a selloff in chip and memory stocks. He also cited the US-Iran war, anxiety before the midterms and rising bond yields. The selloff then spread to South Korea and Taiwan, whose markets those stocks dominate, he said.

“Crypto is widely held in the US, Korea and Taiwan. So naturally, when investors in those regions de-risk, this creates spillover pressures in crypto markets,” Lee said.

Some Bitcoin miners now earn from the AI boom directly. TeraWulf, which built its business mining Bitcoin, signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic in July that it expects to bring in about $19 billion, according to its SEC filing.

The post Was Anthropic’s IPO the Real Reason Behind Bitcoin’s November Crash? appeared first on CryptoPotato.

title: Anthropic's IPO was huge. It also ties the fate of the U.S. economy closer to AI.
description:
The day finally arrived. Anthropic (ANT) began trading on Thursday at $111.50 per share, surging above its $83 IPO price and briefly attaining a market capitalization of $2 trillion before settling into a still-respectable $1.2 trillion. What took years for the tech giants to achieve, the frontier AI lab grabbed in an instant. 
But the historic IPO is notable not just for its size, but also for what it says — and will say — about the makeup of the stock market and the outsized influence of its largest players.
The top 10 biggest companies make up close to 40% of the S&P 500 (^GSPC). A bad day for tech means a bad day for the market. And now that Anthropic has joined the trillion-dollar ticker club — though it won't join the S&P 500 anytime soon — Wall Street's fate is tightly bound with another huge tech company, which also happens to be an AI lab without a long track record of financial stability. 

The top-heavy nature of the S&P 500 means the benchmark index is less diverse than it looks. Sure, investors are buying into a basket of hundreds of names. But since the tickers with the largest market caps get the highest proportional weights, a handful of names can move the entire index.  
That's how you can get such different performances from the equal-weighted S&P 500 (^SPXEW) index (up 11% so far this year) versus the standard, market-weighted version (up 6%).

Big Tech's importance in the stock market has attracted praise and concern for years, even before the arrival of ChatGPT. AI has only deepened that concentration. The tech giants have adopted the AI boom as their new reason for being. And, in a very literal sense, have poured huge investments into their own AI operations and a sprawling ecosystem of chipmakers, LLM suppliers, power generators, and infrastructure firms. 
Anthropic's IPO adds to tech's significance and amplifies the industry's financial gravity. But the frontier lab is also a primary supplier of AI tools. And it counts the country's biggest tech firms as its biggest customers, as well as plenty of other major corporate services. That further intertwines the stock market's top players. 
Digital billboards advertise Anthropic on the day of its IPO in Times Square, New York, on Nov. 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)
AP Photo/Seth Wenig

This recent drama over cyber outages and stories about urgent patches causing havoc also showcases AI tools in action and their myriad risks. And how they're integrated into the economy now — whether companies and users are ready for them. 
And, of course, Anthropic's debut is only the beginning. OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) is coming, and the data center infrastructure boom is still accelerating, further pushing AI chips into the economy's pot. Should the AI boom underdeliver, all that concentration and interconnection will accentuate an AI disappointment into something far bigger. 
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

title: How Bitcoin Treasury Companies Reach Income Investors
description:
In 2025, as bitcoin breached $125,000 and hit a new all-time high, some equity managers were not able to get exposure. Their remits didn’t allow them to hold coins directly…
The post How Bitcoin Treasury Companies Reach Income Investors appeared first on Bitfinex blog.
fullContent:
In 2025, as bitcoin breached $125,000 and hit a new all-time high, some equity managers were not able to get exposure. Their remits didn’t allow them to hold coins directly or own a bitcoin ETF.

Instead, some gained exposure by buying shares in bitcoin treasury companies. Demand was strong enough to allow the largest bitcoin treasury company, Strategy, to raise $25.3 billion, which it says made it the largest issuer of US equity that year, with about eight percent of the total.

But there was another pool of investors that couldn’t access treasury company stock either — fixed-income allocators. It is this market that is now being targeted by bitcoin treasury companies as they exit a turbulent 2026.

“What’s Next for Bitcoin Treasury Companies” panel at the Future of Capital Markets Summit in Lugano. From left: Jesse Knutson (Bitfinex Securities), Alexandre Laizet (Capital B), Matt Cole (Strive), Richard Byworth (BYZ Partners), Raphael Zagury (Twenty One Capital) and Sean Bill (former Co-Founder BSTR).

Preferred Stock Opens the Fixed-Income Market

Fixed income funds generally can’t buy equity and may not be able to buy convertible bonds. Strategy’s Stretch (STRC), launched in 2025, is a dividend-paying preferred stock with a variable annual dividend rate currently set at 12 percent, giving this pool of capital an instrument within their remit.

The premiums on treasury company common stock narrowed during the 2026 downturn but, thanks to the popularity of the preferred instruments, some were able to keep accumulating. Strive raised $630 million in October through a new preferred equity issuance, and STRC has traded close to its $100 par value.

At the 2026 Future of Capital Markets Summit in Lugano, Switzerland, Jesse Knutson, Head of Operations at Bitfinex Securities, chaired a panel in which executives from the sector set out how they are offering bitcoin-style returns, without the volatility. 

Offering new bitcoin-based investments brings more capital into the bitcoin market, which allows treasury companies to issue more common stock. And, as the market for their instruments grows, they become eligible for more investors. The risk is that this virtuous circle depends on bitcoin returning more than the dividend yield pays. In a down year, the flow can reverse. 

As bitcoin fell from above $126,000 last October to below $60,000 in 2026, treasury companies came under pressure. By 24 July VanEck’s Matthew Sigel had counted at least nine that had liquidated or abandoned their strategies. And, by 21 September only four of the 20 largest digital asset treasury companies traded above the value of their holdings. 

The companies that survived came out with stronger balance sheets, cash to cover more than a year of dividend payments and even more bitcoin in their treasury. Strategy has a cash reserve of approximately $4.75 billion and continues bitcoin purchases. In another example, in August, H100 Group more than tripled its holdings to 3,506 bitcoin by acquiring two Norwegian treasury companies in an all-share deal. 

Byworth said the continued interest in bitcoin treasury companies is due to identifying a new gap in the fixed income markets. Investors are resisting yields of around five percent on government debt when they are able to access  large technology company debt at seven to nine percent. Perpetual preferred stock issued by treasury companies pays between 12-13 percent, and the proceeds are used to buy bitcoin. “What the people across this stage are doing is providing the first proper digital credit tool for the fixed-income market”, Byworth said.

“What’s Next for Bitcoin Treasury Companies” panel at the Future of Capital Markets Summit in Lugano.

Tokenisation Reaches Investors Outside US Markets

But what if you could offer these products in a tokenised manner? Preferred stock opened bitcoin exposure to allocators whose mandates ruled out holding bitcoin. Through tokenisation they can be offered to investors who cannot easily reach US-listed securities at all. 

The barriers are geographical and financial. Martin Baumann, co-founder of bitcoin investment firm CMCC Global, said its funds had previously only been open to professional investors, with a minimum subscription of $1 million. 

Bitcoin treasury companies and professionally managed bitcoin strategy companies were recently listed on Bitfinex Securities where they can be bought in fractions of a share. “It gives access to people who otherwise just simply wouldn’t be able to participate,” Baumann said. Offering digital credit products taps one pool of investors barred from participating in bitcoin and tokenising them taps a global pool of investors who can subscribe “with a click of a mouse button”. 

A year after they were among the market’s most watched sectors, bitcoin treasury companies have been through what Byworth called “the first cycle”. It stripped away the premiums that funded their early growth and exposed the companies that had no other way to raise capital. 

The ones still accumulating found one. Digital credit gave Strategy and Strive access to fixed-income allocators who could not hold bitcoin or common stock, and tokenisation is starting to open the same instruments to investors outside US markets. Whether that grows the sector depends on the arithmetic underneath it. 

Preferred stock paying between 12 and 13 percent adds value only if bitcoin returns more than that over time. If it does, every new pool of investors brings more capital into bitcoin, and the companies that came through this year are well positioned for the next wave.
